definition_zh: 到达；送达；到来
definition_en: to reach a place at the end of a journey, or for something to be delivered
core_image: 火车进站，旅客走下车踏上站台
scene: 火车停稳在站台，旅客们提着箱子走下车。 We arrived at the station before noon.
sceneCN: 这里 arrived 是「到达」（第 1 个义项：旅程到达终点）；句意为我们在中午前抵达车站。

senses.title: To reach a place
senses.definition: to reach a place at the end of a journey
senses.definitionCN: 在旅程终点抵达某地
senses.example: We arrived at the station before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在中午前抵达车站。
senses.why: The old phrase meant to reach the shore, so a journey reaching its place is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 古短语意为靠岸，所以旅程到达目的地就是第一义。

senses.title: To be delivered
senses.definition: to come to a person as a letter or a parcel does
senses.definitionCN: 像信件或包裹那样来到某人手中
senses.example: The parcel arrived this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 包裹今天早上送到了。
senses.why: Things also travel and reach a door, so the same verb covers what is delivered.
senses.whyCN: 物品也会旅行并到达门口，所以同一个动词也指送达。

intro.en: The recorded history of arrive is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 arrive 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Ad ripam meant to the shore or to the bank.
items.cn: ad ripam 意为到岸边或到河岸。

items.en: French arriver meant to come to land after a crossing.
items.cn: 法语 arriver 意为渡过后靠岸。

items.en: English borrowed arrive for reaching a place.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪借入 arrive，指抵达某地。

items.en: Later it also covered goods reaching a person.
items.cn: 后来它也指货物送到某人手中。

items.en: Today trains, letters and people all arrive.
items.cn: 今天火车、信件与人都可以用 arrive。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: The third person form of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的第三人称单数形式。

entries.definition: The past form of the verb.
The noun for reaching a place.
It can take a place directly without a preposition.
entries.definitionCN: 可直接接地点，不必加介词。

entries.definition: It stresses movement toward the speaker.
It is used of a plane or a boat touching ground.
entries.definitionCN: 用于飞机或船触地靠岸。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: The Latin phrase meant to the shore: to arrive is to reach land after a crossing.
normal.cn: 拉丁短语意为「到岸边」：arrive 就是渡过之后终于靠岸。

normal.en: The same family also gives arrival and arrivals.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 arrival 与 arrivals。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase arrive at.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「到达（某地）」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of arrive in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 arrive 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: to reach a place at the end of a journey, or for something to be delivered.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「到达」时用它。

definition_zh: 死的；失去生命的；没电的；死寂的
definition_en: no longer alive; without power or activity
core_image: 停止摆动的钟摆
scene: 上课铃响后，手机屏幕黑了怎么按也不亮，原来是彻底没电了。 The phone in his pocket was dead by lunchtime.
sceneCN: 这里 dead 是「没电的」（第 3 个义项：失去功能、不再运作）；句意是到午饭时他口袋里的手机彻底没电了。

derivatives.zh: dead 的基础动词，义为「死；死亡」
由 die 加名词化后缀 -th 构成，义为「死亡」
由 dead 加 -ly 构成，义为「致命的」

senses.title: No longer alive
senses.definition: having no life any more, said of people, animals and plants
senses.definitionCN: 不再有生命，用于人、动物和植物
senses.example: The gardener cut away the dead branches in early spring.
senses.exampleCN: 初春时园丁剪掉了枯死的树枝。
senses.why: When life leaves, movement and warmth leave with it.
senses.whyCN: 生命离开时，活动与温度也一同离去。

senses.title: Without power or function
senses.definition: not working, because it has no power or signal
senses.definitionCN: 因无电或无信号而无法工作
senses.example: The old walkie-talkie went dead during the drill.
senses.exampleCN: 演习时旧对讲机没了声音。
senses.why: A stopped machine is as silent as a stopped heart, so machines borrow the word.
senses.whyCN: 停摆的机器和停止跳动的心一样安静，机器便借用了这个词。

senses.title: Complete silence or stillness
senses.definition: total, with no movement or sound
senses.definitionCN: 完全没有动静或声音
senses.example: A dead silence filled the hall before the results were read.
senses.exampleCN: 公布结果前，大厅里一片死寂。
senses.why: The strongest degree borrows the image of lifelessness.
senses.whyCN: 最高的程度借用了「毫无生气」的画面。

items.en: The verb die grew from Old Norse deyja, to pass away.
items.cn: 动词 die 源自古诺斯语 deyja（离世）。

items.en: The adjective form dead was already in Old English, from Germanic dauþaz.
items.cn: 形容词 dead 已见于古英语，源自日耳曼语 dauþaz。

items.en: The same root dau- appears in the Gothic word for death; the root means to pass away.
items.cn: 同一词根 dau- 也见于哥特语的「死亡」一词，本义为「离世」。

items.en: Noun death and adjective dead settled in their modern jobs.
items.cn: 名词 death 与形容词 dead 各自定型。

items.en: Modern English extends dead to batteries, towns and silence.
items.cn: 现代英语把 dead 扩展到电池、死城和死寂。

note.en: These words belong to the death family or describe stopped things.
note.cn: 这些词属于死亡词族，或描述停摆的事物。

definition_zh: 市场；集市；某种商品的交易领域；销路、需求；股市；行销、推销
definition_en: a place or system in which goods and services are bought and sold, or the willingness of buyers to purchase them
core_image: 清晨的集市街：木棚下摆着成筐的果子，一杆秤搁在摊边，买主与卖主在摊前讨价
scene: 天刚亮，街边木棚下摆满果筐，买卖双方在摊前讨价。 Growers bring their produce to a market where buyers bargain over each crate.
sceneCN: 前半情境：天刚亮，街边木棚下摆满果筐，买卖双方在摊前讨价；句中的 market 指「买卖双方定期相聚的集市场地」（第 1 个义项：作为交易场所的集市）。图中可辨识物件：木棚、果筐、杆秤、写价的木牌。

pos.zh: 市场；集市；交易领域；销路；股市；买方群体
行销；推销；把产品推向市场

senses.title: A place where buyers and sellers meet
senses.titleCN: 买卖双方相聚的集市场地
senses.definition: an open place, often with stalls, where people regularly come together to buy and sell goods
senses.definitionCN: 常设有摊位的露天场所，人们定期在此相聚买卖货物
senses.example: Farmers set up stalls at the weekly market.
senses.exampleCN: 农民每周在集市上摆摊。
senses.why: the Latin noun mercatus named the place and the trading done there, so the word began as a location for exchange.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 mercatus 既指场所也指在那里进行的交易，因此这个词最初就是交换的地点。

senses.title: Trade in one particular commodity
senses.titleCN: 某一种商品的交易领域
senses.definition: the whole body of buying and selling in one commodity or one sector, wherever it happens
senses.definitionCN: 某一种商品或某一部门中全部买卖活动的总和，不论发生在何处
senses.example: The world market for copper tightened last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年世界铜的交易领域收紧了。
senses.why: the place sense was transferred from a square to a field of trade, so that copper can have a market with no square at all.
senses.whyCN: 场所义从一方广场转移到一片交易领域，于是铜可以有市场，而完全不需要广场。

senses.title: Demand for a product
senses.definition: the number of buyers willing to purchase something, or the absence of such buyers
senses.definitionCN: 愿意购买某物的买者数量，或这类买者的缺乏
senses.example: There is little market for hand-written ledgers now.
senses.exampleCN: 如今手写账簿已没什么销路。
senses.why: without buyers a place of exchange is empty, so the word came to mean the willingness to buy rather than the ground it stands on.
senses.whyCN: 没有买主，交换的场所就是空的，于是这个词转而指购买的意愿，而不是它所在的那块地。

senses.title: The market for shares and securities
senses.definition: the organized exchange on which shares, bonds and currencies are traded, or trading there as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 买卖股票、债券与货币的有组织的交易所，或该处的交易整体
senses.example: Share prices fell across the market before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 午前整个股市的股价都下跌了。
senses.why: a stock exchange is a marketplace in the original sense, only with paper claims instead of crates, so the old word was kept.
senses.whyCN: 证券交易所就是原义上的集市，只是货物换成了纸面权益，旧词因此被沿用。

senses.title: Offered for sale
senses.titleCN: 在售；待售（置于售卖状态）
senses.definition: the state of being available to buy, as in a house that has come onto the market
senses.definitionCN: 处于可供购买的状态，如已挂牌出售的房子
senses.example: The building came onto the market in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋楼在春天挂牌出售。
senses.why: being placed before buyers is the modern equivalent of being carried to the stalls, and the phrase on the market keeps that image.
senses.whyCN: 被摆到买主面前，相当于旧时把货物挑到摊位上，这一短语保留了那个画面。

senses.title: To sell and promote a product
senses.definition: to promote and sell a product by choosing its buyers, its price and the way it is presented
senses.definitionCN: 通过选择买主、定价与呈现方式来推销并卖出产品
senses.example: The firm markets its software to schools.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司把软件行销给学校。
senses.why: if a market is where goods find buyers, then to market is to do the work of bringing goods and buyers together.
senses.whyCN: 如果市场是货物找到买主的地方，那么行销就是把货物与买主带到一起的工作。

senses.title: The mechanism that sets prices
senses.definition: the system in which prices and quantities are settled by the competing decisions of many buyers and sellers
senses.definitionCN: 价格与数量由众多买卖双方的竞争性决定来敲定的系统
senses.example: The market, not the ministry, decides which suppliers survive.
senses.exampleCN: 决定哪些供应商存活的是市场，而不是部委。
senses.why: abstracting the place away leaves only its function: bringing competing offers together until a price emerges.
senses.whyCN: 把场所抽掉，只剩它的功能：把互相竞争的报价汇集起来，直到价格出现。

senses.title: The body of intended buyers
senses.definition: the group of people or institutions a seller intends to reach, considered as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 卖方打算触及的那一群人或机构，被作为一个整体来看
senses.example: The brand's market is young urban readers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个品牌的目标买方群体是年轻的城市读者。
senses.why: a seller who studies the crowd at the stalls ends by treating that crowd as an object to be served, which is the marketing sense.
senses.whyCN: 研究摊位前人群的卖方，最终把那群人当作服务对象，这就是营销义。

intro.en: Market is Latin in origin, not a native English word: it goes back to Latin mercatus 'market, trading', a noun from the verb mercari 'to trade', which in turn rests on merx (genitive mercis) 'goods'. It reached Old English through Old Northern French and Germanic channels. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: market 是拉丁来源，而非英语本族词：它上溯至拉丁名词 mercatus「市场、集市、交易」，该名词出自动词 mercari「做买卖」，而动词又基于 merx（属格 mercis）「货物」。它经古北法语与日耳曼中介进入古英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Merx, genitive mercis, meant 'goods, merchandise'. Its own deeper origin is uncertain, and no pre-Latin source can be demonstrated.
items.cn: merx（属格 mercis）意为「货物、商品」。它自身更深的来源不确定，无法证明任何拉丁语之前的源头。

items.en: From the noun came the deponent verb mercari 'to buy and sell, to trade', which names the activity rather than the goods.
items.cn: 由这个名词产生异态动词 mercari「买卖、做交易」，命名的是活动而非货物。

items.en: The noun mercatus 'market, marketplace, trading' was formed on the same stem, so place and activity were one word from the start.
items.cn: 名词 mercatus「市场、集市、交易」由同一词干构成，因此场所与活动从一开始就是一个词。

items.en: The form market is generally thought to have come to England through Old Northern French, with Germanic channels also involved in its spread.
items.cn: 一般认为 market 这一形式经古北法语传入英格兰，其传播也涉及日耳曼中介。

items.en: Old English already had market as a loanword, which is why the word counts as Latin in origin rather than as an inherited native term.
items.cn: 古英语已经以借词形式拥有 market，因此这个词算作拉丁来源，而非承继的本族词。

items.en: From the physical fair the word widened to trade in one commodity, to demand, to the share market and finally to the verb for promoting goods.
items.cn: 从有形的集市出发，这个词扩展到单一商品的交易、需求、股票市场，最后扩展到推销货物的动词义。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin root, so their kinship is real and can be traced; group two holds near neighbours that all name places or gatherings for trade.
note.cn: 第一组的词同出拉丁词根，亲缘关系真实可溯；第二组是同样指交易场所或聚会的近邻词。

entries.definition: Through Old French from Latin mercari: a person who trades, so it shares the root for 'goods' with market and adds an agent suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 经古法语来自拉丁 mercari：做买卖的人，与本词同出「货物」这一词根，只多了一个施事后缀。

entries.definition: From merx 'goods' through Old French: the goods themselves, which is the root meaning in concrete form.
entries.definitionCN: 经古法语来自 merx「货物」：货物本身，正是该词根的具体形态。

entries.definition: From Italian mercante, from Latin mercari: relating to trade, a later borrowing of the same root rather than a new coinage.
entries.definitionCN: 经意大利语来自拉丁 mercari：关于贸易的，是同一词根的后期借入，而非新造词。

entries.definition: Com- 'together' plus merx: trade viewed as an organized exchange between parties, another descendant of the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中表示「共同」的前缀加 merx：把贸易看作各方之间有组织的交换，是同一词根的另一支后裔。

entries.definition: Market plus place: the square or platform where trading happens, narrower than market because it has no demand or share-price senses.
entries.definitionCN: 由 market 与表示「地方」的成分复合而成：发生交易的广场或平台，比本词窄，因为不含需求与股价等义。

entries.definition: From Latin feria 'holiday': a periodic, often seasonal gathering for trade, with none of the abstract economic senses of market.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 feria「节日」：定期、常为季节性的交易聚会，不含本词那些抽象经济义。

entries.definition: From Persian through Turkish: a covered street of shops, a place word only and never a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 经土耳其语来自波斯语：有顶棚的店铺街，只作场所词，从不用作动词。

entries.definition: A shortened form of market kept for names and poetry; it retains only the place sense.
entries.definitionCN: market 的缩略形式，多用于名称与诗歌，只保留场所义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives rather than invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The chain runs goods, then trade, then place: merx, mercari, mercatus.
normal.cn: 链条是货物、交易、场所：merx、mercari、mercatus。

normal.en: The family runs market, marketing, marketplace, marketer, marketable, marketization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 market、marketing、marketplace、marketer、marketable、marketization。

normal.en: Fixed phrases separate the senses: on the market, market share, market forces, stock market.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分开各个义项：在售、市场份额、市场力量、股票市场。

normal.en: The same root shows in merchant, merchandise, mercantile and commerce.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 merchant、merchandise、mercantile 与 commerce 中。

normal.en: The verb takes an object: to market a product, and the -ing form is the noun marketing.
normal.cn: 动词要带宾语：把产品行销出去，其动名词形式就是名词「营销」。

abstract.en: Picture a square that is crowded at dawn and swept clean by noon.
abstract.cn: 想象一方广场，黎明时挤满人，到正午已被扫空。

abstract.en: Picture two columns on a page: what buyers want, and what they will pay.
abstract.cn: 想象纸页上两栏：买主想要什么，愿意付多少。

abstract.en: Picture a board of share prices where one company's fate becomes a single flashing number.
abstract.cn: 想象一块股价牌，一家公司的命运变成一个闪动的数字。

examples.en: The fishing market opens before sunrise and is empty by noon.
examples.cn: 鱼市在日出前开张，到正午便空了。

examples.en: A product with no market cannot survive, however carefully it is made.
examples.cn: 无论做得多用心，没有销路的产品都活不下去。

examples.en: The cooperative markets its coffee directly to roasters abroad.
examples.cn: 这家合作社把咖啡直接行销给国外的烘焙商。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马克」的谐音——集市上每件货物都用马克笔标上价钱 → 市场

root: 拉丁 merx（属格 mercis）「货物」→ 动词 mercari「做买卖」→ 名词 mercatus「市场、集市、交易」→ 经古北法语与日耳曼中介借入古英语 market；merx 更深来源不确定，故为拉丁来源而非英语本族词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one building: goods (merx) are traded (mercari) in a place (mercatus). From the dawn square the line moves to trade in a single commodity, to the demand that fills or empties the square, to the share market that inherited the name, to the state of being offered for sale, to the verb that brings goods and buyers together, to the price-setting mechanism abstracted from the square, and finally to the crowd of buyers a seller sets out to serve.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一座建筑展开：货物在某个场所里被交易。从黎明时的广场出发，这条线依次走向单一商品的交易、决定广场空与满的需求、继承了这个名称的股票市场、被摆出来售卖的状态、把货物与买主带到一起的动词、从广场抽象出来的定价机制，最后走向卖方打算服务的那群买主。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dawn market square where crates change hands and the crowd thins by noon.
core.cn: 核心意象：黎明的集市广场，成筐货物易手，到正午人群渐散。

branches.en: PLACE AND COMMODITY: a square for exchange becomes a field of trade in one good.
branches.cn: 场所与商品：用于交换的广场变成某一种商品的交易领域。

branches.en: DEMAND AND SHARES: buyers make the square alive, and paper claims inherit its name.
branches.cn: 需求与证券：买主让广场有生气，纸面权益则继承了它的名称。

branches.en: OFFER AND PROMOTE: goods are placed before buyers, and someone must bring them there.
branches.cn: 摆出与推销：货物被摆到买主面前，而总得有人把它们带到那里。

branches.en: ALLOCATION: strip away the square and what remains is a mechanism that settles prices.
branches.cn: 配置：把广场抽走，剩下的就是一个敲定价格的机制。

branches.en: BUYER GROUP: the crowd at the stalls becomes the audience a seller intends to reach.
branches.cn: 买方群体：摊位前的人群变成卖方打算触及的对象。

intro.en: The word is a Latin root for 'goods' dressed in noun and verb endings, with English suffixes building the modern family on top.
intro.cn: 这个词是「货物」这一拉丁词根加上名词与动词词尾，再由英语后缀在其上搭起现代词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin merx and its verb mercari supply the stem; mercatus, the noun of place and activity, is the direct ancestor of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 merx 及其动词 mercari 提供词干；指场所与活动的名词 mercatus 则是英语这个词的直接祖先。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of goods in every member of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根为词族中每个成员提供「货物」这一观念。

items.example: Merx names what is carried to the stalls.
items.exampleCN: merx 指被挑到摊位上的东西。

items.structure: mercari, mercatus sum (Latin deponent verb, first conjugation)
items.meaning: to trade, to buy and sell
items.example: The verb turns goods into an activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把货物变成一种活动。

items.example: The noun carries both the place and the dealing.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词同时承载场所与交易。

items.meaning: a place or system of exchange
items.example: Old English already used the borrowed noun.
items.exampleCN: 古英语已经使用这个借入的名词。

items.example: The compound keeps only the place sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词只保留场所义。

items.example: Marketing grew out of the verb to market.
items.exampleCN: 营销由动词「行销」发展而来。

items.meaning: the process or activity of doing
items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a trade activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成一种行业活动。

items.example: Only marketable varieties reached the stalls.
items.exampleCN: 只有可销售的品种被送上摊位。

items.example: The suffix marks what can be sold.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标出能够被卖出之物。

latinEntries.structure: mercari, mercatus sum (deponent verb, first conjugation)
latinEntries.meaning: to trade, to buy and sell

definition_zh: 小时；钟头；时刻；一小时的路程
definition_en: a period of sixty minutes, or a fixed time for something, or the distance reached in an hour
core_image: 钟面上长针走完的一整圈：六十格刻度，不多不少
scene: 图书馆里坐了一个钟头，长针在钟面上转满了一圈。 The library talk lasted an hour, and then we went home.
sceneCN: 这里 hour 是「小时」（第 1 个义项：六十分钟）；讲座持续了整整一小时。

pos.zh: 小时；钟头；时刻（复数指作息时间）

collocations.zh: 在任意（不合时宜的）时刻

derivatives.zh: hour + -ly → 每小时一次的；按小时计的
hour + glass → 沙漏（一小时的玻璃计时器）

senses.title: A period of sixty minutes
senses.definition: a fixed period of sixty minutes used for measuring time
senses.definitionCN: 固定为六十分钟的计时单位
senses.example: We waited almost an hour for the last bus.
senses.exampleCN: 我们等末班车等了将近一小时。
senses.why: The core sense is one full circle of the long hand on the clock face.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是长针在钟面上走满一整圈。

senses.title: A fixed time of day
senses.definition: a particular time of day fixed by habit or rule
senses.definitionCN: 由习惯或规定确定的某一天中的时间
senses.example: Lunch hour is the quietest time in this office.
senses.exampleCN: 午餐时刻是这间办公室最安静的时候。
senses.why: One circle of the clock names the moment it points to: the hour becomes a place in the day.
senses.whyCN: 钟面的一圈同时指出了它停下的位置：小时变成了「一天中的某个地点」。

senses.title: The working or opening times
senses.titleCN: 作息时间；营业时间（复数）
senses.definition: the times when a shop, office or person works or opens (used in the plural)
senses.definitionCN: 商店、机构或个人工作、营业的时间（用复数）
senses.example: The shop’s opening hours are from nine to nine.
senses.exampleCN: 这家商店的营业时间是从九点到九点。
senses.why: The day is divided into named hours, and the set of those names becomes a timetable.
senses.whyCN: 一天被分成有名字的钟点，这些名字的总和就成了作息表。

intro.en: Hour came through Old French houre from Latin hora, an hour, which Greek took from the East.
intro.cn: hour 经古法语 houre 来自拉丁 hora「小时」，希腊语的 hora 又借自东方。

items.en: Greek hora meant season and hour: a division of the day as well as a time of year.
items.cn: 希腊语 hora 兼指时节与钟点：既是时段，也是季节。

items.en: Latin hora meant the twelfth part of daylight, fixed later as sixty minutes.
items.cn: 拉丁 hora 原指白昼的十二分之一，后固定为六十分钟。

items.en: Old French houre carried the word into English after the Conquest.
items.cn: 诺曼征服后，古法语 houre 把该词带入英语。

items.en: Middle English spelled it houre or our; the h began to be pronounced later.
items.cn: 中古英语拼作 houre 或 our，h 起初不发音，后来才读出。

items.en: Modern English built hourly, hourglass and rush hour.
items.cn: 现代英语派生 hourly、hourglass，并造出 rush hour。

note.en: Group one holds silent-h words; group two holds units and moments of time.
note.cn: 第一组是 h 不发音的词；第二组是时间单位与时刻词。

entries.definition: every hour, or paid by the hour
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「每小时一次；按小时计」

entries.definition: a glass timer shaped like two joined cones
entries.definitionCN: hour + glass 复合，义为「沙漏」

entries.definition: belonging to us; sounds the same as hour
entries.definitionCN: our 是物主代词「我们的」，与 hour 同音异义

entries.definition: a period of sixty seconds; one sixtieth of an hour
entries.definitionCN: 分钟，小时的六十分之一

entries.definition: a very short point of time
a period of twenty-four hours

normalIntro.en: Use the silent h and the clock image.
normalIntro.cn: 用不发音的 h 与钟面意象记 hour。

normal.en: hour, honest, honour: three silent-h words
normal.cn: hour、honest、honour：三个 h 不发音的词。

normal.en: an hour, not a hour: it starts with a vowel sound
normal.cn: 说 an hour：hour 以元音开头。

normal.en: hour and our sound the same: your hour, our hour
normal.cn: hour 与 our 同音：你的时刻，我们的时刻。

normal.en: rush hour is when the streets fill up
normal.cn: rush hour＝街道被塞满的时刻＝高峰期。

normal.en: the hour hand is short, the minute hand is long
normal.cn: 时针短，分针长——hour 是短针走过的一圈。

abstract.en: Picture the long hand closing a slow circle and resting.
abstract.cn: 想象长针慢慢合拢一个圆，然后轻轻停住。

abstract.en: Picture sand falling in a glass until the top chamber is empty.
abstract.cn: 想象沙漏里的沙从上格漏空——一小时。

abstract.en: Feel a train ride measured not in kilometres but in hours.
abstract.cn: 把一段车程感受成用小时而非公里来丈量。

examples.en: The doctor will see you in half an hour.
examples.cn: 医生半小时后给你看诊。

examples.en: The museum’s opening hours changed in winter.
examples.cn: 博物馆的开放时间在冬季有变化。

examples.en: They talked hour after hour on the quiet platform.
examples.cn: 他们在安静的月台上聊了一个又一个小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「澳尔」——时针走完一整圈，我们（our）就又过了一 hour（小时），两个词读音正好一样。

root: hour 经古法语 houre 来自拉丁 hora「小时」，拉丁词借自希腊语 hora（时节、钟点），后者又源自东方；属外来词而非日耳曼本族词。

sensesIntro.en: From one full circle of the clock, hour widens to fixed moments and to timetables.
sensesIntro.cn: hour 从钟面的一整圈，扩展到一天中固定的时刻，再到作息与营业时间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the long hand closing one full circle
core.cn: 核心意象：长针合拢的整整一圈

branches.en: the measured block of sixty minutes
branches.cn: 六十分钟的计量块（义项 01）

branches.en: the named moment it points to
branches.cn: 它所指出的有名有姓的时刻（义项 02）

branches.en: the set of moments turned into a timetable
branches.cn: 时刻集合而成的作息表（义项 03）

branches.en: a length of time becomes a place in the day
branches.cn: 一段时长变成一天中的位置（义项 01 · 02）

branches.en: hours as working times
branches.cn: 指工作与营业时间（义项 03）

intro.en: Hour is a small Latin-root noun with a compact English family.
intro.cn: hour 是源于拉丁语的小名词，英语词族紧凑。

latinIntro.en: Latin hora, and Greek hora before it, are the ancestors; horology, the study of timekeeping, shares them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 hora 及其前的希腊 hora 是其祖先；钟表学 horology 也出自同一来源。

items.structure: Old French houre, from Latin hora

items.example: She turned the hourglass over again.

items.meaning: the short hand of a clock
items.example: The hour hand pointed at four.
Leave early to miss the rush hour.
Hora also gave horoscope, hour of birth.
items.exampleCN: hora 还派生 horoscope（出生时刻）。

items.meaning: the study and craft of clocks
items.example: Horology studies every kind of clock.
items.exampleCN: 钟表学研究各类计时器。

definition_zh: 成年人；成年的；成熟的；成体
definition_en: a person or an animal that is fully grown, or fully grown in size
core_image: 成年人在公园里陪孩子玩
scene: 公园里，一位成年人在陪孩子们玩球。 An adult must stay with the children.
sceneCN: 这里 adult 是「成年人」（第 1 个义项：已长大的人）；句意为必须有一位成年人陪着孩子们。

senses.title: A fully grown person
senses.definition: a person who is fully grown and no longer a child
senses.definitionCN: 已经长大、不再是孩子的人
senses.example: Every adult in the hall stood up.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅里的每位成年人都站了起来。
senses.why: Adult is the participle of a Latin verb meaning to grow up, so as a noun it names someone who has finished growing.
senses.whyCN: adult 是拉丁语「长大」动词的分词，作名词就指已经长成的人。

senses.title: Fully grown
senses.definition: of a person, having reached full growth
senses.definitionCN: 指人已达到完全的成长
senses.example: The film is for adult viewers.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影面向成年观众。
senses.why: The same participle used before a noun describes what belongs to grown people.
senses.whyCN: 同一个分词放在名词前，就形容属于成年人的事物。

senses.title: Mature in behaviour
senses.definition: showing the good sense expected of a grown person
senses.definitionCN: 表现出成年人应有的明智
senses.example: She gave an adult answer.
senses.exampleCN: 她给出了成熟的回答。
senses.why: Growing up was applied to behaviour, where it means showing a grown person's good sense.
senses.whyCN: 把「长大」用在言行上，就表示举止成熟。

intro.en: The recorded history of adult is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 adult 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Adultus meant grown up, a participle of the verb to grow.
items.cn: adultus 意为长大的，是表示生长的动词的分词。

items.en: Adolescere meant to grow up, and it gave adolescent as well.
items.cn: adolescere 意为长大，也给出了 adolescent。

items.en: English borrowed adult for a fully grown person.
items.cn: 英语十六世纪借入 adult，指完全长成的人。

items.en: Law later fixed an age when a person counts as adult.
items.cn: 法律后来规定了被视为成年人的年龄。

items.en: Today it also describes films and classes for grown people.
items.cn: 今天它也形容面向成年人的电影与课程。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: More than one grown person.
The period of life when one is grown.
A young person between child and adult.
entries.definitionCN: 指介于儿童与成人之间的青少年。

entries.definition: A friendly word for an adult.
It stresses full development, often of behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 强调完全发展，常指行为。

entries.definition: An older person in a family or a group.
entries.definitionCN: 指家庭或群体中较年长的人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: adultus means grown up, from the verb meaning to grow: an adult has finished growing.
normal.cn: adultus 意为长大的，来自表示生长的动词：adult 就是已经长成的人。

normal.en: The same family also gives adulthood and adulting.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 adulthood 与 adulting。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase an adult ticket.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「成人票」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of adult in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 adult 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: a person or an animal that is fully grown, or fully grown in size.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「成年人」时用它。

abstract.en: Picture a grown person playing with children in a park.
abstract.cn: 想象成年人在公园里陪孩子玩。

abstract.en: The same picture can be literal in one sentence and figurative in another.
abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。

examples.en: Every adult in the hall stood up.
examples.cn: 大厅里的每位成年人都站了起来。

examples.en: The film is for adult viewers.
examples.cn: 这部电影面向成年观众。

examples.en: She gave an adult answer.
examples.cn: 她给出了成熟的回答。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿达尔特」——成年人在公园陪孩子玩球：成年人

root: adult 来自拉丁语 adultus「长大的」，是表示生长的动词的分词，同源词还有 adolescent；英语十六世纪借入，指完全长成的人，法律后来规定了被视为成年人的年龄，今天也形容面向成年人的电影与课程。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of adult grows from one core image: a grown person playing with children in a park.
sensesIntro.cn: adult 的各个义项都从同一个核心意象生长出来：成年人在公园里陪孩子玩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grown person playing with children in a park
core.cn: 核心意象：成年人在公园里陪孩子玩

branches.en: Sense 01 covers the most literal use: A fully grown person.
branches.cn: 义项 01 覆盖最字面的用法：成年人。

branches.en: Sense 02 covers a wider everyday use: Fully grown.
branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更宽泛的日常用法：成年的。

branches.en: Sense 03 covers a further use: Mature in behaviour.
branches.cn: 义项 03 覆盖更靠后的一种用法：行为成熟的。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 02 covers the two main uses: A fully grown person / Fully grown.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 02 覆盖两个主要用法：成年人、成年的。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 03 covers the two main uses: A fully grown person / Mature in behaviour.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 03 覆盖两个主要用法：成年人、行为成熟的。

definition_zh: 组织；机构；企业；编排；整理；组织结构
definition_en: a group of people with a particular purpose and structure, or the act of arranging things into an ordered system
core_image: 一张桌上摊开的机构图，方框之间用直线连成层级，没有一处悬空
scene: 这个国际组织在三个国家设有办事处。 The international organization keeps offices in three countries.
sceneCN: 这个国际组织在三个国家设有办事处；句中的 organization 指「为特定目的而设立的机构」（第 2 个义项：机构、团体）。图中可辨识物件：机构图、办事处门牌、文件夹、地球仪；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 组织；机构；企业；编排；整理；组织结构

senses.title: A group with a purpose and a structure
senses.definition: a group of people working together with defined roles towards a shared aim
senses.definitionCN: 为共同目标而按既定角色协作的一群人
senses.example: Every organization needs someone to keep the records.
senses.exampleCN: 每个组织都需要有人保管记录。
senses.why: The word comes from the Greek word for a tool, and an organization is a group arranged like an instrument for a purpose.
senses.whyCN: 这个词出自希腊语中表示「工具」的词，组织就是为某个目的像器具一样被安排起来的一群人。

senses.title: An institution or body
senses.definition: an established body such as a charity, a union, a hospital or an international agency
senses.definitionCN: 已设立的机构，如慈善团体、工会、医院或国际机构
senses.example: The international organization keeps offices in three countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国际组织在三个国家设有办事处。
senses.why: Once a group acquires a name, rules and premises, it is spoken of as an institution rather than a gathering.
senses.whyCN: 当一群人有了名称、规则与办公场所，人们就说它是机构，而不只是一次聚会。

senses.title: A company treated as a body
senses.definition: a business viewed as a structured body of departments, staff and procedures
senses.definitionCN: 被视为由部门、人员与流程构成的企业
senses.example: The organization employs four hundred people across six sites.
senses.exampleCN: 这家企业在六个地点雇了四百人。
senses.why: Calling a firm an organization shifts attention from its trade to its internal arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 把企业称作 organization，注意力就从它的买卖转到它的内部安排。

senses.title: The act of arranging something
senses.definition: the act of putting parts, events or tasks into a workable order
senses.definitionCN: 把各部分、活动或任务排成可运作次序的动作
senses.example: The organization of the festival took six months.
senses.exampleCN: 节庆的组织工作花了六个月。
senses.why: Before the word meant a body, it meant the act of giving parts an order, and that act still carries the name.
senses.whyCN: 在指团体之前，这个词指「给各部分定次序」的动作，这个动作至今仍用这个名称。

senses.title: The structure itself
senses.definition: the pattern of departments, ranks and reporting lines inside a body
senses.definitionCN: 机构内部部门、层级与汇报线的格局
senses.example: The new director redrew the organization within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 新主管在一年内重画了组织结构。
senses.why: If organizing is giving order, the resulting order is also called by the same name.
senses.whyCN: 如果组织是赋予次序，那么产生的次序也用同一个名称。

senses.title: The quality of being orderly
senses.definition: the quality of doing things in an ordered, planned way
senses.definitionCN: 以有序、有计划的方式做事的性质
senses.example: Her organization kept the whole project on schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 她的条理性让整个项目按计划推进。
senses.why: A person can possess the same order that a body has, so the noun also names a personal capacity.
senses.whyCN: 一个人也可以拥有团体那样的秩序，因此这个名词也指个人能力。

senses.title: The arrangement of living tissue
senses.definition: the structured arrangement of cells and tissues in a living body
senses.definitionCN: 活体中细胞与组织的结构安排
senses.example: The microscope revealed the organization of the leaf tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 显微镜显示出叶片组织的构造。
senses.why: Biology borrowed the word for the ordered arrangement of parts in a living thing, from the same tool image.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用这个词，指活体中各部分有序的安排，仍沿用「器具」的意象。

senses.title: An international body
senses.definition: a body set up by states or by agreement across borders to handle shared matters
senses.definitionCN: 由国家设立或跨国协议建立、处理共同事务的机构
senses.example: The organization was founded to coordinate relief after the war.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国际组织是为协调战后救济而设立的。
senses.why: States needed permanent instruments for shared work, and the tool sense of the root fits that role exactly.
senses.whyCN: 各国需要为共同事务设立常设工具，词根的「器具」义正好契合这一角色。

intro.en: Organization comes from organize, built on Latin organum 'instrument', from Greek organon 'tool'. It first named the act of arranging and later the body so arranged. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: organization 来自 organize，其基础是拉丁 organum「器具」，再溯至希腊 organon「工具」。它先指安排的动作，后指被安排成的团体。年代均为约数。

items.en: Organon meant 'tool, instrument', and Greek philosophy used it for an instrument of reasoning as well as a physical tool.
items.cn: organon 意为「工具、器具」，希腊哲学既用它指推理的工具，也指实物器具。

items.en: Latin borrowed organum for an instrument, and it also named a musical instrument and, later, a bodily organ.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 organum 指器具，也用来指乐器，后来又指身体器官。

items.en: The verb organize meant to give parts an order so that they work together, like fitting tools to a task.
items.cn: 动词 organize 意为给各部分定次序使它们协同运作，像把工具配到一项任务上。

items.en: In English organization first named the act of arranging; by the eighteenth century it named the body that results.
items.cn: 在英语中，organization 先指安排的动作；到十八世纪才指由此形成的团体。

items.en: Industrial and international bodies made the word the standard term for any structured group, from charities to agencies.
items.cn: 工业与国际机构使这个词成为任何有结构团体的标准称呼，从慈善团体到政府机构。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same organ root; group two holds words for structured groups.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「器具」词根的各种形式；第二组是表示有结构团体的词。

entries.definition: To arrange things or people into order; the act behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物或人排成次序；是名词背后的动作。

entries.definition: A part of a body or a musical instrument, from the same tool word; it is not a group.
entries.definitionCN: 指身体器官或乐器，同出「器具」一词；不是团体。

entries.definition: An individual living being, whose parts are organized; it is a creature, not an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个活体，其各部分有组织；是生物，不是机构。

entries.definition: Relating to an organization or its structure; it describes, while organization names.
entries.definitionCN: 与组织或其结构有关的形容词；描述性质，organization 命名实体。

entries.definition: An established body or custom with social standing; it stresses endurance, not internal arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 指有社会地位的既定机构或惯例；强调持久，不强调内部安排。

entries.definition: A group of people joined for a shared interest, usually voluntarily; often smaller than an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 指为共同兴趣自愿结合的一群人；通常比 organization 小。

entries.definition: Any group treated as a unit, such as a governing body; it is vaguer about structure.
entries.definitionCN: 指被当作单位处理的任何群体，如管理机构；对结构说得更含糊。

entries.definition: A business, usually a professional partnership; it cannot name a charity or an agency.
entries.definitionCN: 指企业，通常是专业合伙；不能指慈善团体或政府机构。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词。

normal.en: Greek for tool: a group arranged like an instrument for a purpose.
normal.cn: 希腊语意为「工具」：为某个目的像器具一样被安排起来的一群人。

normal.en: The family runs organize, organization, organizational, organizer and organism.
normal.cn: 同族词有 organize、organization、organizational、organizer 与 organism。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: a non-profit organization, an international organization, the organization of work.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出各义项：非营利组织、国际组织、工作的安排。

normal.en: The same root gives organ, a body part that is itself a tool.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 organ，即本身就是「工具」的身体部件。

normal.en: The word first meant the act of arranging, then the body arranged.
normal.cn: 这个词先指安排的动作，后指被安排成的团体。

abstract.en: Picture a chart of boxes joined by straight lines, none of them floating.
abstract.cn: 想象一张方框图表，方框之间用直线相连，没有一个悬空。

abstract.en: Picture a toolbox where every tool hangs in its own marked place.
abstract.cn: 想象一只工具箱，每件工具都挂在标好的位置上。

abstract.en: Picture a choir that breathes together without anyone shouting.
abstract.cn: 想象一个合唱团，没人喊叫却一起换气。

examples.cn: 这个组织培训志愿者教阅读。

examples.en: Poor organization wasted half the budget.
examples.cn: 糟糕的统筹浪费了一半预算。

examples.en: She is known for her organization and calm under pressure.
examples.cn: 她以有条理和临压不乱而出名。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one instrument: the purposeful group, the institution, the company as a body, the act of arranging, the structure, the personal orderliness, the living tissue, and the international body.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一件「器具」：有目的的团体、机构、作为组织看待的企业、安排的动作、组织结构、个人的条理性、活体组织，以及国际机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an instrument whose parts fit together so that it can do one job.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件器具，各部件互相咬合，从而能完成一项工作。

branches.en: GROUP AS TOOL: a purpose-driven group and a company seen as a body are the same instrument at different legal sizes.
branches.cn: 作为工具的群体：为目的一组人与被视为身体的企业，是同一器具的不同法律规模。

branches.en: LASTING BODY: a charity and an international agency are institutions built to keep working.
branches.cn: 持久的身体：慈善团体与国际机构都是为持续运作而建的机构。

branches.en: FITTING TOGETHER: before there is a body there is the act of giving parts an order.
branches.cn: 装配：在团体存在之前，先有给各部分定次序的动作。

branches.en: THE ORDER ITSELF: the pattern of departments and reporting lines is the result of arranging.
branches.cn: 次序本身：部门与汇报线的格局，是安排的结果。

branches.en: NATURAL ORDER: a tidy person and living tissue both show parts kept in working order.
branches.cn: 自然秩序：有条理的人与活体组织，都显示各部分保持运作秩序。

intro.en: Organization is a Greek tool word plus a Latin action suffix, a common pattern in academic English.
intro.cn: organization 是希腊语「工具」词加拉丁动作后缀，是学术英语中常见的模式。

latinIntro.en: Greek organon passed into Latin as organum, giving organ, organize, organization and organism.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 organon 进入拉丁作 organum，给出 organ、organize、organization 与 organism。

definition_zh: 怀疑；疑问；不确定；怀疑（某事不真）
definition_en: a feeling of not being sure, or to think something may not be true
core_image: 站在岔路口不敢迈步的人
scene: 交卷前最后一秒，他盯着第七题的答案迟迟不肯改。 She had no doubt that her answer was right.
sceneCN: 这里 doubt 是「怀疑、不确定」（第 1 个义项：对真假拿不准的感觉）；句意：她毫不怀疑自己的答案是对的。

derivatives.zh: doubt 加形容词后缀构成，义为「可疑的；不确定的」
doubt 加后缀构成，义为「无疑地」
doubt 加否定前缀再加副词后缀构成，义为「毫无疑问地」

senses.title: Not sure if something is true
senses.definition: a feeling of uncertainty about truth or success
senses.definitionCN: 对真假或成败拿不准的感觉
senses.example: There is some doubt about the date of the event.
senses.exampleCN: 这件事的日期还有些不确定。
senses.why: Latin dubitare means to waver: the mind hesitates between two paths like a walker at a fork.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 dubitare 意为「摇摆」：心在两条路之间犹豫，像站在岔路口的人。

senses.title: Think something may be false
senses.definition: to believe something may not be true
senses.definitionCN: 认为某事可能不真实
senses.example: I doubt that he will come so early.
senses.exampleCN: 我不太相信他会来这么早。
senses.why: Wavering tilts toward disbelief: one of the two paths is chosen in the heart.
senses.whyCN: 摇摆偏向不信：心里的两条路已暗暗选了一条。

senses.title: A reason to question or disbelieve
senses.definition: a reason for questioning a claim
senses.definitionCN: 质疑某个说法的理由
senses.example: The report cast doubt on the old numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 报告让人对旧数据产生了疑问。
senses.why: The inner wavering becomes an outer question that others must answer.
senses.whyCN: 内心的摇摆变成必须由他人回答的外部质疑。

intro.en: Doubt grows from a Latin verb about wavering between two paths.
intro.cn: doubt 长自一个表示「在两条路之间摇摆」的拉丁动词。

items.en: Latin dubitare meant to waver, to hesitate, related to duo, two.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dubitare 意为摇摆、犹豫，与 duo（二）相关。

items.en: Dubius meant doubting, unclear, a mind pulled two ways.
items.cn: dubius 意为可疑的、不清楚的，即被两个方向拉扯的心。

items.en: Old French douter meant to fear and to doubt.
items.cn: 古法语 douter 兼有恐惧与怀疑之义。

items.en: English took doubt around the thirteenth century, keeping the b in spelling.
items.cn: 约十三世纪英语借入 doubt，拼写保留了 b。

items.en: The b stays in spelling though it is silent in speech.
items.cn: 如今 b 在书写中保留，在口语中不发音。

note.en: These words sit near doubt in form or meaning.
note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 doubt 相邻。

definition_zh: 音乐会；演唱会
definition_en: a public performance of music by singers or players
core_image: 舞台上一群乐手同时奏响音乐
scene: 学校艺术节请来民乐团演出。 We are going to a piano concert this Saturday.
sceneCN: 这里 concert 是「音乐会」（第 1 个义项：公开的音乐演出）；句意是周六我们去看钢琴音乐会。

derivatives.zh: 由 concert 加 -ed 构成，义为「一致的；协同的」
由 concert 加 goer 构成，义为「常去听音乐会的人」

senses.title: A public music performance
senses.definition: an event where musicians play or sing for an audience
senses.definitionCN: 乐手或歌手为观众公开演奏、演唱的活动
senses.example: The band played at our school concert.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队在我们的校园音乐会上演出。
senses.why: Musicians working together agreed on one sound, and the agreement became the event.
senses.whyCN: 乐手们商定共奏一音，这份「协同」最终指称整场演出。

senses.title: Working together in agreement
senses.titleCN: 协同；一致（用于短语 in concert）
senses.definition: acting together with others, as in the phrase in concert
senses.definitionCN: 与他人协作行动，见于短语 in concert
senses.example: Police worked in concert with teachers during the event.
senses.exampleCN: 活动期间警方与老师协同工作。
senses.why: The old meaning of agreeing or uniting survives in this phrase.
senses.whyCN: 「商定、联合」的旧义在这个短语里留存下来。

intro.en: Concert began as an agreement between voices.
intro.cn: concert 起于声部之间的「商定」。

items.en: Latin certare meant to strive or contend, with con- adding together.
items.cn: 拉丁语 certare 意为争斗、竞逐，前缀 con- 表示「一起」。

items.en: Italian concerto first meant an agreement or union, then a musical piece with parts agreeing.
items.cn: 意大利语 concerto 先指协议、联合，后指声部协同的乐曲。

items.en: Italian concertare meant to arrange or bring into agreement.
items.cn: 意大利语 concertare 意为安排、协调一致。

items.en: French concert carried the musical performance sense.
items.cn: 法语 concert 承载了「音乐演出」之义。

items.en: Middle English concert first meant agreement or union of people.
items.cn: 中古英语 concert 起初指人们的协议或联合。

items.en: Modern English concert fixed the public music event sense.
items.cn: 现代英语 concert 把「公开音乐演出」固定下来。

note.en: The first group collects words close in spelling; the second collects music events.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写相近的词，第二组收音乐演出相关词。

definition_zh: 计划；打算；平面图；设计
definition_en: an organized idea of what will be done; a drawing of a building or area seen from above; to arrange something in advance; and to design a building or a town
core_image: 一张摊开的纸上，铅笔先画出方框，再写满步骤
scene: 铺开的图纸压住桌角，铅笔在方格之间来回比量。 The council approved the plan for a new library on the corner.
sceneCN: 这里 plan 是「计划、方案」（第 1 个义项：事先安排好的做法）；句意为议会批准了在街角建新图书馆的方案。图中可辨识物件：图纸、铅笔、方格线。

derivatives.zh: 由 plan 双写末尾的 n 再加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「计划者；规划师」
由 plan 加 -ing 构成，义为「规划；计划工作」
由否定前缀 un- 加 planned 构成，义为「未计划的；意外的」

senses.title: An organized idea of what will be done
senses.definition: an organized set of steps or intentions for doing something in the future
senses.definitionCN: 为将来做某事而安排好的步骤或意图
senses.example: The council approved the plan for a new library on the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 议会批准了在街角建新图书馆的方案。
senses.why: The word first named a flat drawing, and a scheme is laid out on paper the way a building is drawn from above, so the flat sheet became the shape of future action.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指一张平面图，而方案也是像俯视建筑那样铺在纸上的，于是平坦的纸面变成了未来行动的轮廓。

senses.title: A drawing of a building seen from above
senses.definition: a drawing that shows the shape and arrangement of rooms, roads or land as if seen from directly above
senses.definitionCN: 像从正上方俯视那样，画出一座建筑、一片街区或一块土地的布局
senses.example: The architect spread the plan across the table.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑师把平面图摊在桌上。
senses.why: Because Latin planum meant a flat surface, the drawing of a floor laid out flat is the oldest physical sense, and it still names what builders work from.
senses.whyCN: 因为拉丁语 planum 意为平坦的面，把楼层平铺画出来就是最古老的实物义，至今仍指施工所依据的那张图。

senses.title: To arrange something in advance
senses.definition: to decide and arrange in advance what one will do or how something will be done
senses.definitionCN: 事先决定并安排好要做什么或怎样做
senses.example: We plan to leave before the traffic builds up.
senses.exampleCN: 我们打算在车流变多之前出发。
senses.why: The verb turns the sheet of intentions into an activity: to plan is to keep laying out the steps the way the drawing lays out the rooms.
senses.whyCN: 动词把那纸意图变成一种活动：plan 就是像图上铺开房间那样，不断把步骤铺排出来。

senses.title: To design a building or a town
senses.definition: to design the layout of a building, a district or a town
senses.definitionCN: 设计一座建筑、一片街区或一座城镇的布局
senses.example: The whole district was planned around a central square.
senses.exampleCN: 整个街区都是围绕一个中央广场规划出来的。
senses.why: When the flat drawing is put to work on real ground, the same word moves from describing a layout to deciding it.
senses.whyCN: 当那张平面图被用到真实的地面上，同一个词就从「描画布局」变成「决定布局」。

intro.en: Plan comes from Latin planus, flat, and planum, a flat surface; the flat drawing gave French and then English the word for a scheme.
intro.cn: plan 来自拉丁语 planus（平的）与 planum（平面）；正是这张平铺的图，把「方案」这个意思给了法语，再给了英语。

items.en: Planus meant flat, level or even, and it described ground that had no bumps in it.
items.cn: planus 意为平的、平坦的、齐平的，用来形容没有起伏的地面。

items.en: The noun planum named a flat surface or level ground, and from it came the idea of a drawing laid out flat.
items.cn: 名词 planum 指平坦的表面或平地，由此生出「平铺开来的图」这一想法。

items.en: French plan used the word for a ground plan, the flat drawing of a building or a camp seen from above.
items.cn: 法语 plan 用这个词指平面图，即从上方俯视建筑或营地的平铺图。

items.en: English borrowed plan for such a drawing and soon extended it to any arranged scheme of action.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 plan 指这类图纸，很快又扩展到任何安排好的行动方案。

items.en: Modern English keeps the drawing, the scheme and the verb of intending, and adds planned towns and planned economies.
items.cn: 现代英语保留图纸、方案与表示打算的动词，并加上规划城镇、计划经济这类说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin adjective for flat, plus two that only share letters; the near-meaning group gathers words for a scheme or a schedule.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「平」这个形容词上的词，另收两个只是字母相像的词；近义组收表示方案与日程的词。

entries.definition: A living thing that grows in soil; the source is Latin planta, a sprout or a sole, not planus.
entries.definitionCN: 在土里生长的生物；来源是拉丁语 planta（嫩芽、脚掌），并不是 planus，只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: A large or slightly secret plan for achieving something.
entries.definitionCN: 为达成某事而设计的大计划或略带隐秘的安排。

entries.definition: A planned piece of work with a clear aim.
entries.definitionCN: 有明确目标的计划性工作。

entries.definition: A list or timetable of things to be done at set times.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定时间安排事务的清单或时间表。

entries.definition: A drawing or arrangement showing how something will be made.

normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「平」的形容词上，整族词都带着「铺在平整纸面上」的画面。

normal.en: Latin planus means flat, so a plan began as a flat drawing rather than a thought in the head.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 planus 意为平的，所以 plan 最初是一张平铺的图，而不是脑子里的念头。

normal.en: A floor plan is the oldest kind of plan, and it still means a view of a building from directly above.
normal.cn: floor plan 是最古老的一种 plan，至今仍指从正上方俯视建筑所得的图。

normal.en: The verb doubles the final n: planned and planning, to keep the short vowel of plan.
normal.cn: 动词变化时末尾的 n 双写：planned、planning，以保持 plan 的短元音。

normal.en: Planner adds -er to the stem and names the person, while planning names the activity.
normal.cn: planner 在词干后加 -er 指人，planning 则指这项活动。

normal.en: According to plan means everything is going the way the sheet said it would.
normal.cn: according to plan 意为一切都按那张纸所写的那样进行。

abstract.en: A plan is a flat drawing of time, with rooms replaced by steps.
abstract.cn: 计划是一张关于时间的平面图，把房间换成了步骤。

abstract.en: To plan ahead is to trust that a sheet of paper can stand in for a stretch of the future.
abstract.cn: 提前计划，就是相信一张纸能够代替一段尚未到来的时间。

abstract.en: The same word draws a building and decides a life, because both begin as lines on a level surface.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既画建筑也安排人生，因为两者都从平整面上的一堆线开始。

examples.en: The council approved the plan for a new library on the corner.
examples.cn: 议会批准了在街角建新图书馆的方案。

examples.en: We plan to leave before the traffic builds up.
examples.cn: 我们打算在车流变多之前出发。

examples.en: The whole district was planned around a central square.
examples.cn: 整个街区都是围绕一个中央广场规划出来的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「铺烂」——图纸铺烂了也要把方案画完；记住 plan 是计划。

root: 拉丁语 planus（平的）与 planum（平面）经法语 plan（平面图）进入英语：先指俯视的图纸，再指事先安排好的方案。plant 与 plantation 来自另一个拉丁词 planta（嫩芽、脚掌），与 plan 只是拼写相近，并非同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a layout drawn on a flat surface; the senses run from the drawing of a building, to a scheme of action, to intending, and finally to designing a district.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是画在平面上的布局；义项从建筑图纸，走到行动方案，再到打算，最后落到规划一片街区。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pencil tracing rooms on a sheet laid flat, then writing steps in the same frame.
core.cn: 核心意象：铅笔在摊平的纸上勾出房间，又在同样的方框里写下步骤。

branches.en: a list of steps pinned above a desk
branches.cn: 钉在书桌上方的步骤清单

branches.en: a floor plan spread under a pencil
branches.cn: 铅笔下摊开的平面图

branches.en: a drawing turning into a timetable
branches.cn: 图纸变成时间表

branches.en: two people agreeing when to leave
branches.cn: 两个人商量什么时候出发

branches.en: streets laid out around one square
branches.cn: 围绕一个广场铺开的街道

intro.en: The word is a Latin adjective of flatness turned into a French noun of drawing, and English adds the usual endings for people and activities.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示「平」的形容词，变成法语里表示图纸的名词，英语又给它加上表示人与活动的常见词尾。

latinIntro.en: Two Latin forms are recorded behind this word: the adjective planus, flat, and the noun planum, a flat surface.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后有两个可考的拉丁形式：形容词 planus（平的）与名词 planum（平面）。

definition_zh: 聋的；失聪的；不愿听的
definition_en: unable to hear, completely or partly; unwilling to listen
core_image: 安静世界里挥动的双手
scene: 学校手语社团招新，展板前同学们跟着视频学简单的问候手势。 My deaf classmate taught us to sign good morning.
sceneCN: 这里 deaf 是「失聪的」（第 1 个义项：听不见或听力受损）；句意是我的听障同学教我们用手语打「早上好」。

derivatives.zh: 由 deaf 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「耳聋；失聪」
由 deaf 加动词后缀 -en 构成，义为「使震耳欲聋」

senses.title: Unable to hear
senses.definition: not able to hear at all, or only partly, because of damage to the ears
senses.definitionCN: 因耳朵受损而完全或部分听不见
senses.example: Deaf fans enjoyed the concert through the vibrations of the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 失聪的观众通过地板的震动欣赏音乐会。
senses.why: When a door of the senses closes, the word records which door it was.
senses.whyCN: 感官之门关闭时，这个词记录下是哪一扇门。

senses.title: Unwilling to listen
senses.definition: refusing to listen to advice, warnings or requests
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝听从劝告、警告或请求
senses.example: He turned a deaf ear to our warnings about the icy path.
senses.exampleCN: 他对我们关于结冰路面的警告充耳不闻。
senses.why: The closed ear can be by choice, so refusal borrows the same word.
senses.whyCN: 耳朵可以因选择而「关闭」，拒绝便借用了同一个词。

intro.en: Deaf is an old Germanic word about closed ears.
intro.cn: deaf 是个关于「闭上的耳朵」的古老日耳曼词。

items.en: deaf already meant unable to hear in Old English.
items.cn: 古英语的 deaf 已经表示听不见。

items.en: It comes from a Germanic root also seen in related words for empty or dull; the exact picture is uncertain.
items.cn: 它出自日耳曼词根，该词根也见于表示「空、钝」的词；具体画面不确定。

items.en: Spelling settled as deaf, pronounced with a short vowel.
items.cn: 拼写定型为 deaf，读短元音。

items.en: The idiom turn a deaf ear spread in common speech.
items.cn: 习语 turn a deaf ear 在民间话语中流行。

items.en: Modern usage prefers deaf people and hearing-impaired in careful language, plus compounds like tone-deaf.
items.cn: 现代用语在正式场合用 deaf people、hearing-impaired，另有 tone-deaf（五音不全）等复合词。

note.en: These words belong to the hearing family or describe closed senses.
note.cn: 这些词属于听觉词族，或描述关闭的感官。

entries.definition: the state of being deaf
to make unable to hear by loud noise
no longer alive; one letter apart from deaf
entries.definitionCN: 死的（与 deaf 一字母之差）

entries.definition: to give out cards or make agreements; spelled close
entries.definitionCN: 交易；发牌（拼写近似，词义无关）

entries.definition: polite way to say partly deaf
unable to see
unable to speak
with reduced but not lost hearing
hand language used by deaf people

normalIntro.en: Watch the ea vowel and pair the word with sign language.
normalIntro.cn: 注意 ea 元音，并与手语搭配记忆。

normal.en: deaf reads DEF, not DEEF; keep the vowel short.
normal.cn: deaf 读 DEF，不是 DEEF，保持短元音。

normal.en: turn a deaf ear to = refuse to listen.
normal.cn: turn a deaf ear to ＝ 充耳不闻。

normal.en: the deaf means deaf people as a group.
normal.cn: the deaf 指聋人群体。

normal.en: deafness is the noun; deafen is the verb about loud noise.
normal.cn: deafness 是名词；deafen 是指巨大声响的动词。

normal.en: Spelling set: dead, deaf, deal, dear all one letter apart.
normal.cn: 拼写组：dead、deaf、deal、dear 各差一字母。

abstract.en: Picture hands flying through sentences in the air.
abstract.cn: 想象双手在空中「说」出整句话。

abstract.en: Feel the bass of drums through your feet at a concert.
abstract.cn: 体会音乐会上鼓点透过脚底的震动。

abstract.en: See a warning letter left unopened on the desk.
abstract.cn: 看桌上那封没有拆开的警告信。

examples.en: The library offers sign-language story time for deaf children.
examples.cn: 图书馆为失聪儿童提供手语故事时间。

examples.en: Loud concerts can leave your ears half deaf for a day.
examples.cn: 吵闹的音乐会可能让你的耳朵半天听不清。

examples.en: Don't turn a deaf ear to the teacher's safety tips.
examples.cn: 别对老师的安全提示充耳不闻。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「代夫」——听不见喊声，只能请人「代」为传「夫」话，因为他 deaf

root: 来自古英语 deaf（听不见），出自日耳曼词根（一般认为与「空、钝」有关，具体画面不确定）；现代正式用语倾向 deaf people / hearing-impaired。

sensesIntro.en: From ears that cannot hear to ears that choose not to.
sensesIntro.cn: 从听不见的耳朵，到选择不听的耳朵。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands speaking where sound cannot
core.cn: 核心意象：安静世界里挥动的双手

branches.en: Hearing fully or partly lost
branches.cn: 全部或部分失去听力

branches.en: Ignoring advice
branches.cn: 不理会劝告

branches.en: Closed ears, by chance or by choice
branches.cn: 偶然或有意关闭的耳朵

branches.en: Sign language and inclusion
branches.cn: 手语与包容

branches.en: Parallel senses: blind, mute
branches.cn: 平行的感官词：blind、mute

intro.cn: deaf 用朴素的英语后缀构词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词根，这个词属于日耳曼语系。

definition_zh: 喊叫；呼喊声；喝斥；请客喝饮料
definition_en: to say something very loudly, a loud cry, to speak angrily, or to buy someone a drink
core_image: 一个人双手拢在嘴边，朝远处用力喊话
scene: 别在图书馆里大喊。 Do not shout in the library.

senses.title: To call loudly
senses.definition: to say something in a very loud voice
senses.definitionCN: 用非常大的声音说话
senses.example: Do not shout in the library.
senses.exampleCN: 别在图书馆里大喊。
senses.why: This is the central action sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的动作义项。

senses.title: A loud cry
senses.definition: a loud call or cry
senses.definitionCN: 响亮的呼唤或喊声
senses.example: We heard a shout from the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 我们听到山上传来一声呼喊。
senses.why: The action turns into a countable event.
senses.whyCN: 动作转化为可计数的事件。

senses.title: To speak angrily
senses.definition: to speak sharply or angrily to someone
senses.definitionCN: 严厉或愤怒地对某人说话
senses.example: He shouted at the driver.
senses.exampleCN: 他冲着司机大吼。
senses.why: Loudness becomes a sign of anger.
senses.whyCN: 大声变成了愤怒的标志。

senses.title: To treat someone
senses.definition: to buy a drink or meal for someone
senses.definitionCN: 为某人买饮料或饭菜
senses.example: I will shout you a coffee.
senses.exampleCN: 我请你喝杯咖啡。
senses.why: A friendly British and Australian use of the word.

items.en: Skuta may have meant a taunt or a call.
items.cn: skuta 可能意为嘲弄或呼喊。

items.en: Shouten meant to call out loudly.
items.cn: shouten 意为大声呼喊。

items.en: The noun shout named a loud cry.
items.cn: 名词 shout 指响亮的喊声。

items.en: Angry speech became a common sense.
items.cn: 愤怒的说话方式成为常见义项。

items.en: British and Australian English added the treating sense.

note.en: Shout is compared with similar-looking words and with words for loud calls.

normalIntro.en: A shout is a voice pushed across a distance.
normalIntro.cn: shout 是把声音推向远处的力量。

normal.en: Do not shout in the library.
normal.cn: 别在图书馆里大喊。

normal.en: We heard a shout from the hill.

normal.en: He shouted at the driver.

abstract.en: A friendly shout can be warmer than a whisper.

root: 可能源自古诺尔斯语 skuta（嘲弄、呼喊），核心义「把声音用力送出去」。

sensesIntro.en: Shout means to call loudly, a loud cry, to speak angrily, or to treat someone.
sensesIntro.cn: shout 意为大声喊叫、呼喊声、喝斥或请客。

core.en: A voice thrown with force toward someone far away.
core.cn: 用力把声音投向远处的人。

branches.en: The voice rises to reach far.

definition_zh: 物体；物品；对象；目的；宾语；反对
definition_en: a thing that can be seen and touched; also the focus of attention or an aim, a grammatical noun that receives the action of a verb, and, as a verb, to express disagreement
core_image: 一件可以拿在手里的东西，被托到眼前，也随时能挡回去
scene: 清晨的库房里，管理员把收到的旧物一件件摆上长桌，登记重量与年份。 The curator lifted each object and wrote its weight in a notebook.
sceneCN: 这里 object 是「物体、物品」（第 1 个义项：能看见、能拿起来的实物）；句意为管理员拿起每一件器物，把重量记在本子上。图中可辨识物件：长桌、旧物、笔记本。

pos.zh: 物体；物品；对象；目的；宾语

derivatives.zh: 由 object 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「反对；异议」
由 object 加 -ive 构成，义为「目标；客观的」
由 objective 加 -ity 构成，义为「客观性」
由 object 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -or 构成，义为「反对者」
由 objection 加后缀 -able 构成，义为「令人反感的；可反对的」

senses.title: A thing that can be seen and touched
senses.definition: a solid thing that exists in the physical world and can be seen or handled
senses.definitionCN: 存在于物质世界、能看见或拿在手里的实体
senses.example: A small object rolled under the table and stopped at her feet.
senses.exampleCN: 一个小东西滚到桌下，停在她脚边。
senses.why: Latin objectum names what has been thrown before the eyes, so the physical thing is the first thing this word ever pointed at.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 objectum 指「被抛到眼前的东西」，所以能看见的实物是这个词最初指向的对象。

senses.title: The focus of attention or feeling
senses.definition: a person or thing toward which attention, interest or a feeling is directed
senses.definitionCN: 注意力、兴趣或情感所指向的人或物
senses.example: The old house became the object of every photographer's attention.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老房子成了每个摄影师关注的对象。
senses.why: Once something is thrown before the mind, it can hold the mind there; the physical thing turns into whatever attention is aimed at.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西既然被抛到心里，就能把心思留住；实物于是转成「注意力瞄准的那个东西」。

senses.title: An aim that a plan is meant to reach
senses.definition: the aim that a plan or an action is meant to achieve
senses.definitionCN: 计划或行动想要达到的那一点
senses.example: The committee met with the object of cutting waiting times.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会开会，目的是缩短等候时间。
senses.why: An aim is also something placed in front of you to move toward, so the word shifts from what is looked at to what is worked for.
senses.whyCN: 目标也是放在你前方、要你走过去的东西，于是词义从「被看着的物」转到「为之努力的终点」。

senses.title: The noun that receives a verb's action
senses.definition: in grammar, the noun or pronoun that the action of a verb is done to
senses.definitionCN: 语法上，承受动词动作的名词或代词
senses.example: In the sentence she wrote the letter, the noun letter is the object.
senses.exampleCN: 在「她写了那封信」这句话里，名词 letter 是宾语。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the word because the object is the thing placed before the verb's action, receiving what is done to it.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用这个词，因为宾语正是被放到动词动作前面的东西，承受着被做的动作。

senses.title: To say that you disagree
senses.definition: to say that you do not agree with or approve of something
senses.definitionCN: 表示不同意或不赞成某事
senses.example: Several neighbours objected to the plan for a new car park.
senses.exampleCN: 好几位邻居反对新建停车场的方案。
senses.why: Latin obicere meant to throw something against someone, and an objection is a word thrown back at a proposal; the modern verb keeps that gesture of standing in the way.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 obicere 意为把东西朝某人扔过去，而反对就是把一句话扔回给一个提议；这个现代动词保留了「挡在前面」的动作。

intro.en: Object comes from Latin words for throwing something before or against; the same root splits into a noun for what is placed in view and a verb for speaking against it.
intro.cn: object 来自拉丁语「把东西抛到前面或对着扔」的说法；同一条词根分成两支，一支指摆在眼前的物，一支指对着说的反对。

items.en: Jacere meant to throw or to cast, and it lies under the -ject of many English words.
items.cn: jacere 意为投、掷，它藏在许多英语词的 -ject 一段里。

items.en: Obicere joined ob-, against or in front of, with jacere, so it meant to throw something in someone's way and also to throw a charge against a person.
items.cn: obicere 把表示对着、在前面的 ob- 与 jacere 合起来，意为把东西抛到某人面前，也指对某人提出责难。

items.en: Objectum, the thing thrown before the mind, came to name whatever is presented to thought, and later the target of a feeling or an aim.
items.cn: objectum 指被抛到心里的东西，用来指呈现在思想面前的一切，后来又指情感或目标所指向的靶子。

items.en: Old French took object as something perceived or opposed, and English borrowed it with both a noun and a verb in view.
items.cn: 古法语把这词用作「被感知之物」与「被反对之物」，英语借用时就同时看到了名词与动词两条路。

items.en: Modern English separates the two by stress: the noun keeps the first syllable strong, the verb moves the beat to the end, and grammar adds the sense of a verb's object.
items.cn: 现代英语用重音把两者分开：名词重音在前，动词重音挪到后面；语法上又添出「动词宾语」一义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same -ject stem from jacere; the near-meaning group gathers words for physical things and for speaking against something.
note.cn: 形近组收同一条 jacere 词干上的 -ject 词；近义组收表示实物与出言反对的词。

entries.definition: A statement or feeling of disagreement.
entries.definitionCN: 表示不同意的话或情绪；异议。

entries.definition: An aim, or something judged without personal feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 目标，或不受个人情感影响的。

entries.definition: A planned piece of work, or to throw something forward.
entries.definitionCN: 有计划的工作，或向前投射。

entries.definition: To put a liquid into the body with a needle.
Any physical item or matter.
One separate article in a list or a set.
entries.definitionCN: 列表或成套物品中单独的一件。

entries.definition: To say publicly that something is wrong.
To speak or act against a plan or an idea.
entries.definitionCN: 出言或行动反对某个计划或想法。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin verb for throwing, so every sense is some version of something placed in front of someone.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词长在表示「投掷」的拉丁动词上，所以每个义项都是「某样东西被放到某人面前」的某种变形。

normal.en: Jacere is Latin for throw, and the -ject in object, project and inject all comes from it.
normal.cn: jacere 在拉丁语里是投掷，object、project、inject 里的 -ject 都出自它。

normal.en: Object and objection share one root, but object names the thing in front of you while objection names the words thrown back.
normal.cn: object 与 objection 同根，但 object 指摆在眼前的物，objection 指扔回去的话。

normal.en: The noun takes the stress on the first syllable and the verb on the second, a split English made to keep the two jobs apart.
normal.cn: 名词把重音放在第一音节，动词放在第二音节，这是英语为了把两件事分开而做的切分。

normal.en: With the object of is a fixed phrase meaning with the aim of, because an object can be a goal.
normal.cn: with the object of 是固定说法，意为以……为目的，因为 object 可以是目标。

normal.en: Object to is followed by a noun or an -ing form, because the preposition to blocks the plain infinitive.
normal.cn: object to 后面接名词或动名词，因为介词 to 挡住了光秃秃的不定式。

abstract.en: Anything you can point at, anything you aim at, and anything you say against a plan are all, in this word, something placed in front of you.
abstract.cn: 你能指着的东西、你瞄准的东西、你对着计划说的话，在这个词里都是「被放到你面前的东西」。

abstract.en: The same root that throws a stone in someone's path also throws a thought before the mind.
abstract.cn: 同一条词根，既把石头扔到别人路上，也把一个念头扔到心里。

abstract.en: A word that names both a pebble and a protest shows how often disagreement begins with simply seeing something in the way.
abstract.cn: 一个既能指小石子、又能指抗议的词，说明不赞同常常始于「看见有东西挡在路上」。

examples.en: A small object rolled under the table and stopped at her feet.
examples.cn: 一个小东西滚到桌下，停在她脚边。

examples.en: Several neighbours objected to the plan for a new car park.
examples.cn: 好几位邻居反对新建停车场的方案。

examples.en: The committee met with the object of cutting waiting times.
examples.cn: 委员会开会，目的是缩短等候时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥不借它」——东西递到眼前偏说不借；object 既是眼前之物，也是出言反对。

root: 一般认为来自拉丁语 objectum（被抛到眼前之物），源于 obicere（对着投掷），由 ob-（对着）加 jacere（投掷）构成，经古法语 object 进入英语；名词与动词重音不同。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something thrown in front of you; from that one gesture come the physical thing, the target of attention, the aim in view, the grammatical receiver and the words spoken against a plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被抛到你面前的东西」；同一个动作长出实物、注意力的靶子、眼前的目标、语法上的承受者，以及对着计划说出的话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a solid thing held up before the eyes, and a hand raised to push it away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件实物被托到眼前，随即有一只手把它推回去。

branches.cn: 小东西滚到桌下看不见的地方

branches.en: an old house drawing every camera in the street
branches.cn: 一座老房子引来街上所有的镜头

branches.en: a meeting called to shorten the wait at a stop
branches.cn: 为缩短站上等候时间而开的会

branches.en: the noun that takes what the verb does
branches.cn: 承受动词动作的那个名词

branches.en: neighbours standing up to speak against a plan
branches.cn: 邻居们站起来反对一个方案

intro.en: The word is Latin ob- plus jacere, and its English branch grows through endings that turn the stem into a noun of action and an adjective of judgement.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语的 ob- 加 jacere，它的英语分支靠后缀长成表示动作的名词与表示判断的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin jacere, to throw, and its compounds obicere and objectum are the recorded source of this word, whose stem also underlies project and inject.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 jacere（投掷）及其复合词 obicere、objectum 是这个词语有记录的来源，它的词干也支撑着 project 与 inject。

definition_zh: 成就；成绩；完成；达到
definition_en: something done well after effort, or the act of reaching a goal
core_image: 领奖台上举起的奖杯
scene: 颁奖礼上，学生从校长手里接过奖杯。 Winning the prize was a real achievement.
sceneCN: 这里 achievement 是「成就」（第 1 个义项：经过努力做成的事）；句意为赢得这个奖是一项真正的成就。

pos.zh: 名词：成就；成绩；完成；达到

senses.title: A great result
senses.definition: something important done through effort
senses.definitionCN: 靠努力做成的重要事情
senses.example: Winning the match was a great achievement.
senses.exampleCN: 赢得比赛是一项了不起的成就。
senses.why: The ending -ment can name the result of the verb achieve, so the word first means a great result.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ment 可以指动词 achieve 的结果，所以这个词先表示了不起的成果。

senses.title: The act of reaching a goal
senses.definition: the act of reaching a goal
senses.definitionCN: 达到某个目标这件事
senses.example: The achievement of the goal took three years.
senses.exampleCN: 实现这个目标用了三年。
senses.why: The same ending can also name the act itself, which gives the sense of reaching a goal.
senses.whyCN: 同一个后缀也可以指动作本身，于是有了「达到目标」这一层意思。

senses.title: A record of success
senses.definition: a record of success in study or work
senses.definitionCN: 学习或工作中成功的记录
senses.example: Her achievements in science won a prize.
senses.exampleCN: 她的科学成绩赢得了一个奖项。
senses.why: When the results are listed together in study or work, achievement means a record of success.
senses.whyCN: 把成果放在学习或工作里排成记录，achievement 就指成绩与成就。

intro.en: The recorded history of achievement is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 achievement 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Achever meant to finish, and the noun grew from that verb.
items.cn: achever 意为完成，名词由这个动词而来。

items.en: English formed the verb achieve, then added a noun ending.
items.cn: 英语先构成动词 achieve，再加名词词尾。

items.en: The ending -ment named the result of the action.
items.cn: 词尾 -ment 指这一行动的结果。

items.en: The noun achievement named a completed feat.
items.cn: 名词 achievement 指完成的功业。

items.en: Today it covers school results and lifetime awards.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖学业成绩与终身成就奖。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: More than one success or result.
The verb meaning to reach a goal.
A person who reaches goals.
It stresses a task fully finished.
A general word for doing well.
It stresses something difficult that was done.

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: achieve means to bring something to its end, and -ment names what has been done.
normal.cn: achieve 意为把事情做到头，-ment 表示已经做成的事。

normal.en: The same family also gives achieve and achiever.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 achieve 与 achiever。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase a great achievement.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「伟大的成就」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of achievement in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 achievement 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: something done well after effort, or the act of reaching a goal.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「成就」时用它。

abstract.en: Picture a cup held high on a winner's stand.
abstract.cn: 想象领奖台上举起的奖杯。

abstract.en: The same picture can be literal in one sentence and figurative in another.
abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。

examples.en: Winning the match was a great achievement.
examples.cn: 赢得比赛是一项了不起的成就。

examples.en: The achievement of the goal took three years.
examples.cn: 实现这个目标用了三年。

examples.en: Her achievements in science won a prize.
examples.cn: 她的科学成绩赢得了一个奖项。

root: achievement 由动词 achieve 加名词词尾 -ment 构成。achieve 来自古法语 achever「完成、做到头」，由 a-「向」与 chief「头」构成；-ment 表示这一行动的结果，今天这个词涵盖学业成绩与终身成就奖。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of achievement grows from one core image: a cup held high on a winner's stand.
sensesIntro.cn: achievement 的各个义项都从同一个核心意象生长出来：领奖台上举起的奖杯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup held high on a winner's stand
core.cn: 核心意象：领奖台上举起的奖杯

branches.en: Sense 01 covers the most literal use: A great result.
branches.cn: 义项 01 覆盖最字面的用法：一项成就。

branches.en: Sense 02 covers a wider everyday use: The act of reaching a goal.
branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更宽泛的日常用法：达到目标的过程。

branches.en: Sense 03 covers a further use: A record of success.
branches.cn: 义项 03 覆盖更靠后的一种用法：成绩记录。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 02 covers the two main uses: A great result / The act of reaching a goal.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 02 覆盖两个主要用法：一项成就、达到目标的过程。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 03 covers the two main uses: A great result / A record of success.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 03 覆盖两个主要用法：一项成就、成绩记录。

intro.en: achievement can be split into the parts below, which also connect it to common English patterns.
intro.cn: achievement 可以按下面的成分拆开，这些成分也把它与常见的英语构词方式连起来。

latinIntro.en: No recorded Latin cognate is securely attached to this word, so the list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠记录的拉丁同族词可以系在这个词上，因此该列表留空。

items.exampleCN: 它标记朝终点去的方向。

items.example: It gives the sense of reaching the top.
items.exampleCN: 它提供到达顶端的意思。

items.example: It names the result of an action.
It marks a plural noun in English.

items.exampleCN: 它标记过去时或已完成的状态。

items.example: It forms the present participle of a verb.
items.exampleCN: 它构成动词的现在分词。

items.example: It turns an adjective into an adverb.

items.exampleCN: 它指做某动作的人或物。

definition_zh: 海；海洋；大量；海面
definition_en: the large body of salt water covering much of the earth, a large amount, or the state of the waves
core_image: 蓝色海面一直延伸到天际，白色浪花一层层涌上沙滩
scene: 孩子们光着脚跑向海边。 The children ran barefoot toward the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 sea 是「海；海洋」（第 1 个义项）；句意：孩子们光着脚跑向海边。

senses.title: The salt water body
senses.definition: the large body of salt water that covers much of the earth
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖地球大部分表面的巨大咸水体
senses.example: The sea was calm at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明时海面很平静。
senses.why: The central sense is the great body of salt water.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是巨大的咸水体。

senses.title: A huge amount
senses.definition: a very large number or amount of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物数量极多的一大片
senses.example: A sea of people filled the square.
senses.exampleCN: 广场上挤满了人海。
senses.why: A boundless expanse becomes an image of great quantity.
senses.whyCN: 无边无际的景象成为数量的比喻。

senses.title: The state of the waves
senses.definition: the condition of the waves on the sea
senses.definitionCN: 海面上波浪的状况
senses.example: The ship sailed into rough seas.
senses.exampleCN: 船驶入了波涛汹涌的海面。
senses.why: The place sense narrows to the water's surface condition.
senses.whyCN: 场所义缩小为水面状况。

intro.en: Sea comes from Old English sæ, a word shared with other Germanic languages.
intro.cn: sea 源自古英语 sæ，与其他日耳曼语言同源。

items.en: Sæ meant the sea or a large lake.
items.cn: sæ 意为海或大湖。

items.en: See named the great body of salt water.
items.cn: see 指巨大的咸水体。

items.en: Sea appeared in many compounds for travel and trade.
items.cn: sea 大量出现在航海与贸易复合词中。

items.en: A sea of something became a common image of quantity.
items.cn: a sea of 成为表示数量的常见比喻。

items.en: Sea means the ocean, its surface, or a vast amount.
items.cn: 现代英语中 sea 指海洋、海面或大量。

note.en: Sea is compared with similar short words and with words for large waters.
note.cn: 把 sea 与形近短词以及表示大片水域的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Sea is the salt water, its waves, and any vast expanse.
normalIntro.cn: sea 是咸水、海浪，也是任何广阔的景象。

normal.en: Sea and see sound the same.
normal.cn: sea 与 see 发音相同。

normal.en: By the sea means near the coast.
normal.cn: by the sea 意为在海边。

normal.en: Sea level is the height of the ocean surface.
normal.cn: sea level 是海平面高度。

normal.en: Seafood comes from the sea.
normal.cn: 海鲜来自海洋。

normal.en: A sea of faces means a huge crowd.
normal.cn: a sea of faces 指人山人海。

abstract.en: A boundless surface easily becomes a metaphor for quantity.
abstract.cn: 无边无际的表面很容易成为数量的比喻。

abstract.en: The same word names the water, its waves, and its scale.
abstract.cn: 同一个词命名水体、波浪与规模。

abstract.en: Sea connects geography with feeling.
abstract.cn: sea 把地理与情感连接起来。

examples.en: The sea was calm at dawn.
examples.cn: 黎明时海面很平静。

examples.en: They live by the sea.
examples.cn: 他们住在海边。

examples.en: A sea of people filled the square.
examples.cn: 广场上挤满了人海。

dict_mnemonic.text: sea 是「海」，与 see 同音；seaside 是海滨，seafood 是海鲜，sea level 是海平面。

sensesIntro.cn: sea 意为海洋、大量，或海面波浪状况。

core.en: A vast body of salt water.
core.cn: 巨大的咸水体。

branches.en: The ocean itself.
branches.cn: 海洋本身。

branches.en: A crowd or amount like an ocean.
branches.cn: 像海洋一样的数量或人群。

branches.en: The movement and mood of the water.
branches.cn: 水面的运动与状态。

branches.en: The vast body inspires images of scale.
branches.cn: 巨大的水体激发规模想象。

branches.en: Water and waves are one experience.
branches.cn: 海水与波浪是同一体验。

intro.en: Sea forms compounds for coast, travel, and food.
intro.cn: sea 构成表示海岸、航海与食物的复合词。
