definition_zh: 重要性；重要地位；显要
definition_en: the quality of being important, or the state of having great value or influence
core_image: 秤上压弯指针的一块重物
scene: 校长在广播里强调安全。 The headmaster stressed the importance of wearing helmets.
sceneCN: 这里 importance 是「重要性」（第 1 个义项：价值或影响的程度）；句意：校长强调佩戴头盔的重要性。

senses.title: The quality of mattering
senses.definition: the degree to which something matters or has value
senses.definitionCN: 某事物有价值或有影响的程度
senses.example: She understands the importance of sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 她明白睡眠的重要性。
senses.why: The scale weighs things: some press the needle hard.
senses.whyCN: 秤在称量事物：有些东西把指针压得很重。

senses.title: Consequence or influence
senses.definition: having power to affect outcomes
senses.definitionCN: 具有影响结果的力量
senses.example: A minister spoke with quiet importance.
senses.exampleCN: 部长说话带着不张扬的威望。
senses.why: What weighs heavily can move people and events.
senses.whyCN: 分量重的东西能推动人与事。

senses.title: A prominent social position
senses.definition: high rank or social standing
senses.definitionCN: 高位或显赫的社会地位
senses.example: The city grew in wealth and importance.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市在财富与地位上崛起。
senses.why: The weight of a name lifts its owner above the crowd.
senses.whyCN: 名字的分量把主人抬到人群之上。

senses.title: Exaggerated self-regard
senses.definition: an exaggerated sense of one's own worth
senses.definitionCN: 对自身价值的夸大感受
senses.example: His self-importance annoyed the team.
senses.exampleCN: 他的自我膨胀让团队恼火。
senses.why: The scale tips toward oneself: weight claimed, not earned.
senses.whyCN: 秤盘偏向自己：宣称的重量，而非挣来的。

intro.en: Importance comes from Latin importare, to carry in or to signify, with the sense of a thing bringing its weight with it. Old French and English import and importance developed the meaning of significance.
intro.cn: importance 来自拉丁语 importare「带入、意味着」，含事物自带分量之义。古法语与英语的 import、importance 发展出「意义、重要性」的含义。

items.en: Latin importare joined in-, in, and portare, to carry: to carry in, then to mean or signify.
items.cn: 拉丁语 importare 由 in「入」加 portare「携带」构成：带入，继而指意味、表明。

items.en: Medieval Latin importantia named the significance or weight of a thing.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 importantia 指事物的意义或分量。

items.en: Old French importer carried the verb into French with the signifying sense.
items.cn: 古法语 importer 以「表明」义把动词传入法语。

items.en: Middle English import meant to convey or signify; importance followed in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 中古英语 import 意为传达、表明；importance 于十五世纪随之出现。

items.en: Modern English settled the value sense and added self-importance in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 现代英语固定价值义，并于十八世纪加入 self-importance。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the import family and a false cousin. The meaning group compares weight and significance words.
note.cn: 形近组收录 import 词族与一个假表亲；词义组比较表示分量与意义的词。

entries.definition: having great value or influence.
to bring in goods; also, the meaning of a text.
lacking power. Starts the same but comes from a Latin word for power, not carrying.
entries.definitionCN: 无力的。开头相同，但源自拉丁语「权力」一词。

entries.definition: the quality of having meaning or consequence.
entries.definitionCN: 意义；重要性。偏指意味与后果。

entries.definition: importance or influence, used metaphorically.
entries.definitionCN: 分量。比喻用法指重要性。

entries.definition: fame or notice; standing out.
entries.definitionCN: 显要。指引人注目、地位突出。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split importance into import + ance, contrast importance and importance-self, and reuse of great importance.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把 importance 拆成 import 加 ance，对照 self-importance，并复用 of great importance。

normal.en: import + ance: what a thing carries in is its importance.
normal.cn: import 加 ance：事物带来的东西就是它的重要性。

normal.en: attach importance to is the fixed verb pattern for valuing something.
normal.cn: attach importance to 是「重视某事」的固定动词句型。

normal.en: self-importance is weight claimed without a scale.
normal.cn: self-importance 是未经称量就自报的重量。

normal.en: importance is the noun; important is the adjective; do not swap them.
normal.cn: importance 是名词，important 是形容词，不要互换。

normal.en: A matter of no importance carries no weight at all.
normal.cn: a matter of no importance 毫无分量。

abstract.en: One image: a tiny key outweighing a mountain of junk.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：一把小钥匙压过一座垃圾山。

abstract.en: Importance is influence per unit of size.
abstract.cn: 重要性是单位体积的影响力。

abstract.en: Beware the mirror: importance felt is not importance measured.
abstract.cn: 当心镜子：感觉到的重要性不等于量出的重要性。

examples.en: Teachers stress the importance of reading aloud.
examples.cn: 老师们强调朗读的重要性。

examples.en: The port lost its importance after the war.
examples.cn: 战后该港失去了重要地位。

examples.en: He spoke with the importance of a general.
examples.cn: 他带着将军般的威望说话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「一破腾斯」：一把重物把秤盘压破腾起，说明它太重要。

root: 拉丁语 importare「带入、表明」（in 入 + portare 携带）→ 中世纪拉丁语 importantia「分量、意义」→ 古法语 → 中古英语 importance「重要性、显要」。

sensesIntro.en: Importance measures how much a thing carries: its value, its influence, its social weight, and the false weight of self-regard.
sensesIntro.cn: importance 衡量事物的承载量：价值、影响力、社会分量，以及自我膨胀的假重量。

core.en: The weight a thing brings in with it, felt on the scale of events.
core.cn: 事物随之带入的分量，在事件的秤上被感知。

branches.en: VALUE: the importance of sleep or study.
branches.cn: 价值：睡眠或学习的重要性。

branches.en: INFLUENCE: speaking with quiet importance.
branches.cn: 影响：带着不张扬的威望说话。

branches.en: RANK: a city rising in importance.
branches.cn: 地位：一座城市的崛起。

branches.en: VANITY: self-importance without earned weight.
branches.cn: 虚荣：未经挣得的自我重要感。

branches.en: ASSESSMENT: attaching importance to what matters.
branches.cn: 评估：重视真正要紧的事。

intro.en: Importance is import plus -ance; the family adds important, importantly and the compound self-importance.
intro.cn: importance 由 import 加 -ance 构成；词族加上 important、importantly 与复合词 self-importance。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the carrying verb that split into trade goods and significance.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示那个分裂为「货物进口」与「意义分量」的携带动词。

items.example: The importance of the match drew huge crowds.
items.exampleCN: 这场比赛的重要性吸引了大批观众。

items.meaning: to bring in goods; to mean

items.example: The error seemed unimportant at first.
items.exampleCN: 起初这错误看似无关紧要。

items.example: This is the importantest rule in dialect speech.

definition_zh: 负担得起；抽得出；承受得起；提供
definition_en: to have enough money or time for something, or to provide something
core_image: 拿起价格牌，算一算钱够不够
scene: 商店里，女孩拿起价格牌，算了算自己的钱够不够。 We cannot afford a new bike this year.
sceneCN: 这里 afford 是「负担得起」（第 1 个义项：有足够的钱做某事）；句意为今年我们买不起新自行车。

pos.zh: 动词：负担得起；抽得出；承受得起；提供

senses.title: To have enough money
senses.definition: to have enough money for something
senses.definitionCN: 有足够的钱用于某物
senses.example: We cannot afford a new car.
senses.exampleCN: 我们买不起新车。
senses.why: The old verb meant to put forward or to supply, and having enough to supply the cost became the sense of being able to pay.
senses.whyCN: 古动词意为「推进、供应」，拿得出所需的钱，就成了买得起。

senses.title: To have enough time or strength
senses.definition: to have enough time or strength for something
senses.definitionCN: 有足够的时间或力气应付某事
senses.example: Can you afford the time for a trip?
senses.exampleCN: 你抽得出时间去旅行吗？
senses.why: The same idea of having enough was applied to time and strength, not only to money.
senses.whyCN: 「拿得出」不只用在线钱上，用在时间与力气上，就是承担得起。

senses.title: To provide something
senses.definition: to give or supply something, in a formal style
senses.definitionCN: 以正式语体给出或供应某物
senses.example: The trees afford welcome shade.
senses.exampleCN: 这些树提供了宜人的阴凉。
senses.why: The oldest sense of supplying something survives in a formal style.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的「供应」义保留在正式语体里，就是提供。

intro.en: The recorded history of afford is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 afford 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: The old verb meant to carry out or to manage a thing.
items.cn: 这个古动词意为完成或设法应付一件事。

items.en: It also came to mean to supply or to provide.
items.cn: 它也发展出供应或提供的意思。

items.en: Later it came to mean having enough for a cost.
items.cn: 后来它表示有足够的钱应付开销。

items.en: The word settled as afford in the modern form.
items.cn: 这个词固定为现代形式 afford。

items.en: Today it covers money, time and risk alike.
items.cn: 今天它可指金钱、时间与风险。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: The third person form of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的第三人称单数形式。

entries.definition: The past form of the verb.
The adjective meaning not too costly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为价格不高的。

entries.definition: It stresses coping with a cost or a task.
It stresses giving up time or money.
It stresses supplying something needed.

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: The old verb meant to get done or to manage, so afford is being able to manage a cost.
normal.cn: 古动词意为把事情办成或设法应付，所以 afford 就是能应付一项开销。

normal.en: The same family also gives affordable and affordability.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 affordable 与 affordability。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase can afford.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「负担得起」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of afford in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 afford 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: to have enough money or time for something, or to provide something.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「负担得起」时用它。

abstract.en: Picture picking up a price tag and working out whether the money is enough.
abstract.cn: 想象拿起价格牌，算一算钱够不够。

abstract.en: The same picture can be literal in one sentence and figurative in another.
abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。

examples.en: We cannot afford a new car.
examples.cn: 我们买不起新车。

examples.en: Can you afford the time for a trip?
examples.cn: 你抽得出时间去旅行吗？

examples.en: The trees afford welcome shade.
examples.cn: 这些树提供了宜人的阴凉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿福德」——拿起价格牌算钱够不够：负担得起

root: afford 来自古英语 afforthian「完成、设法应付」，也发展出供应与提供的意思，后来表示有足够的钱应付开销；这个词固定为现代形式 afford，今天可指金钱、时间与风险。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of afford grows from one core image: picking up a price tag and working out whether the money is enough.
sensesIntro.cn: afford 的各个义项都从同一个核心意象生长出来：拿起价格牌，算一算钱够不够。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: picking up a price tag and working out whether the money is enough
core.cn: 核心意象：拿起价格牌，算一算钱够不够

branches.en: Sense 01 covers the most literal use: To have enough money.
branches.cn: 义项 01 覆盖最字面的用法：买得起。

branches.en: Sense 02 covers a wider everyday use: To have enough time or strength.
branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更宽泛的日常用法：承担得起。

branches.en: Sense 03 covers a further use: To provide something.
branches.cn: 义项 03 覆盖更靠后的一种用法：提供。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 02 covers the two main uses: To have enough money / To have enough time or strength.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 02 覆盖两个主要用法：买得起、承担得起。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 03 covers the two main uses: To have enough money / To provide something.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 03 覆盖两个主要用法：买得起、提供。

intro.en: afford can be split into the parts below, which also connect it to common English patterns.
intro.cn: afford 可以按下面的成分拆开，这些成分也把它与常见的英语构词方式连起来。

latinIntro.en: No recorded Latin cognate is securely attached to this word, so the list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠记录的拉丁同族词可以系在这个词上，因此该列表留空。

items.example: It is a form of the prefix before f.
items.exampleCN: 它是该前缀在 f 前的变体。

items.example: It gives the sense of managing a thing.
items.exampleCN: 它提供设法应付的意思。

items.example: It marks a plural noun in English.
It marks the past tense or a completed state.
items.exampleCN: 它标记过去时或已完成的状态。

items.example: It forms the present participle of a verb.
items.exampleCN: 它构成动词的现在分词。

items.example: It turns an adjective into an adverb.
It names the doer of an action.
items.exampleCN: 它指做某动作的人或物。

items.example: It turns an adjective into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成表状态的名词。

definition_zh: 语言；言语；（某一领域的）表达方式；计算机语言
definition_en: a system of spoken or written signs used for communication, or a particular style or code of expression
core_image: 一张围着许多人的旧木桌，桌上摊着写满不同文字的纸页，几个人正用手势和声音相互回应
scene: 旧木桌旁围坐着来自几座村镇的人，桌上摊着写满不同文字的纸页。 Language was the only tool they had in common that afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里指「用于交流的声音与符号系统」（第 1 个义项：人类交流的整体系统）；句意为那天下午，语言是他们唯一共同拥有的工具。可辨识物件：旧木桌、纸页、不同文字、手势。

pos.zh: 语言；言语；表达方式（可数与不可数两用）

senses.title: The human system of communication
senses.titleCN: 人类用于交流的符号系统
senses.definition: the shared system of sounds, words and grammar by which people communicate
senses.definitionCN: 人们借以交流的声音、词汇与语法的共享系统
senses.example: Language is learned in company, not from a dictionary alone.
senses.exampleCN: 语言是在与人相处中学到的，而不是只靠词典。
senses.why: the word came from the Latin name for the tongue, so the oldest image is the organ that produces speech.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语对「舌头」的称呼，因此最古老的画面是发出言语的器官。

senses.title: A particular named tongue
senses.definition: a specific system such as Chinese, Arabic or Swahili, counted as one item
senses.definitionCN: 如汉语、阿拉伯语或斯瓦希里语等具体系统，可作为一个单位计数
senses.example: She speaks four languages and reads two more.
senses.exampleCN: 她会说四种语言，还能读另外两种。
senses.why: once the general capacity was recognized, each separate system needed the same name.
senses.whyCN: 当整体能力被认出之后，每一个独立的系统也需要同一个名称。

senses.title: Speech as it is actually used
senses.definition: the spoken words of a person or group on a given occasion, as opposed to writing
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某群体在某一场合说出的具体话语，与书面语相对
senses.example: His language in the meeting was far plainer than his letters.
senses.exampleCN: 他在会上说的话比他的书信朴素得多。
senses.why: the tongue is the instrument of speech, so the word also names the spoken output itself.
senses.whyCN: 舌头是说话的器官，因此这个词也指说出来的产物。

senses.title: The style and wording of a text
senses.definition: the choice of words and sentence patterns that gives a text its tone
senses.definitionCN: 使文本形成某种语气的用词与句式选择
senses.example: The language of the report was careful but cold.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告的措辞谨慎而冷淡。
senses.why: a text's manner of speech can be described with the same word used for a nation's tongue.
senses.whyCN: 一个文本的说话方式，可以用描述民族语言的同一个词来指称。

senses.title: The vocabulary of a special field
senses.titleCN: 某一专业的行话与术语
senses.definition: the technical words and conventions used by a profession or subject
senses.definitionCN: 某职业或学科使用的术语与惯例
senses.example: Legal language keeps ordinary readers at a distance.
senses.exampleCN: 法律行话把普通读者挡在门外。
senses.why: a profession speaks its own tongue, so its terms are called a language.
senses.whyCN: 一个职业说自己的话，因此其术语被称作一种语言。

senses.title: A code for machines
senses.definition: a formal set of instructions that a computer can process
senses.definitionCN: 计算机可以处理的一套形式化指令
senses.example: The course teaches one programming language at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课一次只教一种编程语言。
senses.why: the word was extended to any rule-governed code, including one no human speaks.
senses.whyCN: 这个词被扩展到任何有规则的代码，包括没有人说的那种。

senses.title: Non-verbal signals
senses.definition: meaning carried by gesture, posture or tone rather than words
senses.definitionCN: 由手势、姿态或语气而非词语承载的意义
senses.example: Her body language said more than her answer.
senses.exampleCN: 她的肢体语言比回答说明了更多。
senses.why: meaning is carried without the tongue at all, and the word follows the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 意义完全不经舌头而传递，词也跟着意义走。

senses.title: The human capacity for speech
senses.titleCN: 人类拥有语言的天赋能力
senses.definition: the general human ability to acquire and use a grammar, studied as a faculty
senses.definitionCN: 人类习得并使用语法的总体能力，被当作一种官能来研究
senses.example: Language separates human communication from simple signalling.
senses.exampleCN: 语言使人类交流区别于简单的信号传递。
senses.why: the most abstract sense returns to the original faculty that makes every other sense possible.
senses.whyCN: 最抽象的义项回到那项使其他所有义项成为可能的原初官能。

intro.en: Language comes from Old French langage, from Latin lingua 'tongue, language'. The further origin of lingua is not established. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词来自古法语 langage，再上溯拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」。lingua 更早的来源未获证明。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lingua meant both 'tongue' and 'language'. The sense grew from the organ to what the organ produces, a common pattern in many languages.
items.cn: lingua 兼指「舌头」与「语言」。词义从器官转到器官的产物，这在许多语言中都是常见模式。

items.en: The deeper origin of lingua is unsettled. A link sometimes proposed with a verb meaning 'to lick' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: lingua 更深的来源没有定论。有人提出它与一个表「舔」的动词有关，那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Old French langage named speech and the way one speaks; English borrowed it in the age of Norman rule.
items.cn: 古法语 langage 指言语及说话方式；英语在诺曼统治时期借入。

items.en: Middle English used the word for a nation's tongue and for a person's manner of speech, both senses surviving today.
items.cn: 中古英语用这个词指一个民族的语言，也指个人的说话方式，两义都留存至今。

items.en: Modern technical life extended the word to formal codes, giving programming languages, and to gesture, giving body language.
items.cn: 现代技术生活把词扩展到形式化代码，产生「编程语言」，也扩展到姿态，产生「肢体语言」。

items.en: Source uncertain: no attested pre-Latin form of lingua is agreed, and the exact route through French is reconstructed from later records.
items.cn: 来源不确定：lingua 在拉丁语之前的形式没有公认书证，经法语传入的确切路径亦由较晚记录构拟。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same root that are often confused; group two holds near neighbours that name communication.
note.cn: 第一组是同根而常被混淆的词；第二组是表示交流的近义词。

entries.definition: Describes what relates to language; it never names the system itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述与语言有关的性质，本身不指那套系统。

entries.definition: The scientific study of language, not a language and not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 指对语言的科学研究，既不是一种语言，也不是一个人。

entries.definition: A person who studies language, or loosely one who knows several.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究语言的人，或宽泛地指通晓多种语言的人。

entries.definition: An informal word for a foreign language or a jargon; it is playful where language is neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 指外语或行话的口语说法，语气戏谑，而「语言」一词为中性。

entries.definition: The act or occasion of speaking; it covers sound but not writing or the abstract system.
entries.definitionCN: 指说话的行为或场合，覆盖声音，却不含书面语或抽象系统。

entries.definition: An old word for a language, as in the mother tongue; it is close but archaic in most uses.
entries.definitionCN: 指语言的旧说法，如「母语」；意思接近，但多数用法已古旧。

entries.definition: One variety within a language; calling it a language is a political judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 指一种语言内部的变体；称它为「语言」常是政治判断。

entries.definition: Any system of signs with rules, including machines; it lacks the human and social weight of language.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何有规则的符号系统，包括机器；缺少语言的人类与社会分量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'tongue', so the word begins as the body part that makes speech.
normal.cn: 词根意为「舌头」，因此这个词最初就是制造言语的身体部位。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: foreign language, body language, programming language.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围：外语、肢体语言、编程语言。

normal.en: The adjective, the discipline and the person all come from the same root.
normal.cn: 形容词、学科与人都出自同一词根。

normal.en: The family runs linguistic, linguistics, linguist, multilingual, bilingual.
normal.cn: 同族包括「语言的」「语言学」「语言学家」「多语的」「双语的」。

normal.en: Counting languages uses the plural, speaking in general uses the singular.
normal.cn: 数具体语言用复数，泛指说话能力用单数。

abstract.en: Picture a table where every sheet is written in a different hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，每张纸都出自不同的笔迹。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge built from sounds rather than stones.
abstract.cn: 想象一座用声音而非石头搭成的桥。

abstract.en: Picture a key ring that opens a different door for every listener.
abstract.cn: 想象一串钥匙，对每个听者打开不同的一扇门。

examples.en: Language changes faster in cities than in isolated valleys.
examples.cn: 语言在城市里的变化比在封闭山谷中更快。

examples.en: The two communities share a border but not a language.
examples.cn: 这两个社群共享一条边界，却不共享一种语言。

examples.en: Nurses are trained to read the body language of anxious patients.
examples.cn: 护士受过训练，能读懂焦虑病人的肢体语言。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「兰格维吉」——拦住陌生人开口，靠的就是这套声音与符号的系统。

root: 拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」经古法语 langage 进入英语；词义由器官转向器官的产物。lingua 更深来源不确定，与表「舔」动词的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses spread from one organ: the tongue produces speech, speech becomes a named system, that system takes styles and jargons, and the same word is finally lent to machines and to silent gesture.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个器官铺开：舌头产生言语，言语成为具名的系统，系统又生出风格与行话，最后同一个词被借给机器与无声的姿态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one table, many scripts, and hands answering in gesture and sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张桌子、多种文字，人们用手势与声音相互回应。

branches.en: THE CAPACITY: the human faculty and its shared system are the two sides of one coin.
branches.cn: 能力：人类的官能与共享系统是同一枚硬币的两面。

branches.en: COUNTED TONGUES: each separate system can be named and counted.
branches.cn: 可数的语言：每一套独立系统都可被命名与计数。

branches.en: BEYOND WORDS: actual speech and silent gesture both carry meaning.
branches.cn: 超出词语：实际说出的话与无声的姿态都承载意义。

branches.en: TONE OF A TEXT: word choice alone can make writing warm or cold.
branches.cn: 文本的语气：仅靠选词就能让文字变暖或变冷。

branches.en: RULED CODES: a profession's jargon and a machine's instructions are both governed sets.
branches.cn: 有规则的代码：专业行话与机器指令都是受规则支配的集合。

intro.en: The word is a French-shaped noun built on a Latin root meaning 'tongue', and that root also builds the whole linguistic family.
intro.cn: 这个词是经法语成形的名词，建在拉丁语表「舌头」的词根上，这个词根也构成整个「语言」词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin lingua gives language, linguist and linguistics through French and Latin endings; the same root appears in the adjective for 'tongue-shaped'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lingua 经法语与拉丁词尾衍生出「语言」「语言学家」与「语言学」；同一词根也出现在表「舌形」的形容词里。

items.meaning: the organ of speech, and speech itself
items.example: The root already carries both the body part and its product.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根已同时带着器官与其产物。

items.example: Language is older than any dictionary.
items.exampleCN: 语言比任何词典都古老。

items.example: The linguist recorded the last speakers.
items.exampleCN: 这位语言学家记录了最后的说话者。
语言证据为这份文本定了年代。
语言学成为一门大学学科。

items.example: Bilingual signs appeared at the airport.

items.exampleCN: 这座城市以多语并存为荣。

items.example: The manual is full of technical lingo.
items.exampleCN: 这本手册满是技术行话。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 双舌的；使用两种语言的

definition_zh: 是否；不管…（还是…）；会不会（两件事中的哪一件）
definition_en: used to introduce two or more possibilities, especially a yes or a no, when the answer is not known
core_image: 岔路口立着一块牌子，一边写「是」一边写「否」
scene: 车停在岔路口，司机摇下车窗问路，路边只有一块牌子：一边是「是」，一边是「否」。 I do not know whether he will come tomorrow.
sceneCN: 这里 whether 是「是否」（第 1 个义项：引出知道与否尚未确定的一件事）；句意为我不知道他明天是否会来。岔路口一边「是」一边「否」的牌子就是这个词的印象。

collocations.zh: 不管是出于偶然还是有意

senses.title: Yes or no
senses.definition: used to name two choices, usually whether something is so and whether it is not
senses.definitionCN: 引出两个选择，通常指某事成立与不成立
senses.example: I do not know whether he will come tomorrow.
senses.exampleCN: 我不知道他明天是否会来。
senses.why: The word began as the Old English interrogative about two things, and the yes-or-no branch is the same fork seen without an answer.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源于古英语对两件事物的疑问，是与否两岔就是同一个岔口，只是没有答案。

senses.title: Either of two
senses.definition: used before two alternatives to say that neither one changes the result
senses.definitionCN: 用在两个并列选项前，表示两者都不改变结果
senses.example: Whether by accident or design, the paper arrived on the very last day.
senses.exampleCN: 不管是偶然还是有意，论文恰好在最后一天到了。
senses.why: When the two branches both lead to the same outcome, the fork stops being a question and becomes a condition.
senses.whyCN: 当两条岔路通向同一结果时，岔口不再问句，而成了一个条件。

senses.title: The question of if
senses.titleCN: 会不会；是否如此（作疑问的名词从句）
senses.definition: used after a verb of asking, knowing or doubting to introduce the matter in doubt
senses.definitionCN: 用在询问、知道、怀疑等动词之后，引出存疑的那件事
senses.example: They are still arguing about whether the plan is legal.
senses.exampleCN: 他们仍在争论这个计划是否合法。
senses.why: A reported question loses its question mark, and whether is the word left holding the doubt.
senses.whyCN: 转述的问句丢掉了问号，whether 就成了那个承载疑问的词。

intro.en: Whether is the Old English pair hwæther or hwæder, which of two, and it has kept that fork-shaped meaning for more than a thousand years.
intro.cn: whether 源自中古前的古英语 hwæther / hwæder（两者中的哪一个），一千多年里一直保留这种分岔的意义。

items.en: The stem hwa- asked about a pair, unlike the plain what that asked about any thing.
items.cn: 词干 hwa- 问的是一对中的哪一个，与询问任何事物的 what 不同。

items.en: Hwæther was the word for which of the two, and it could open a question or a clause.
items.cn: hwæther 是「两者中哪一个」的说法，既能开启问句，也能引出一个从句。

items.en: The final r weakened and was often dropped before a consonant, which gave the modern spelling and pronunciation.
items.cn: 词尾的 r 变弱，在辅音前常被吞掉，于是形成今天的拼写与读音。

items.en: The fixed pair whether or no (later whether or not) settled the alternative pattern in print.
items.cn: 固定的搭配 whether or no（后来作 whether or not）把这种两选句式固定在书面语里。

items.en: Grammar books sorted whether and if apart, keeping whether for careful writing and after prepositions.
items.cn: 语法书把 whether 与 if 分工，让 whether 留在严谨的文章和介词之后。

note.en: The first group collects the words that share the same wh shape, the second the words that also offer a choice or a condition.
note.cn: 第一组收与它字形相近的 wh 词，第二组收同样引出选择或条件的说法。

entries.definition: Not a question word at all, but the state of the sky.
entries.definitionCN: 天气（与 whether 读音几乎相同）

entries.definition: To dry up and shrink, one vowel apart.
The old word for to what place.
A different opening letter, meaning to a certain degree.
Can also mean whether, but never after a preposition.
One of the two, the older partner of whether.
Marks a doubt instead of naming the two branches.
Covers the either-or sense: it does not matter which.

normalIntro.en: Think of a road sign with two arrows, one saying yes and one saying no, and the word is the sign itself.
normalIntro.cn: 想一块画着两支箭头、一支写「是」一支写「否」的路牌，这个词就是那块牌子。

normal.en: Whether and weather sound the same, but one asks about a choice and one about the sky.
normal.cn: whether 与 weather 同音，但一个问选择，一个说天空。

normal.en: Whether or not: the or not is the second branch, made explicit.
normal.cn: whether or not：那个 or not 就是把第二条岔路说出来。

normal.en: After a preposition only whether works, as the decision was about whether to go.
normal.cn: 介词之后只能用 whether，例如决定是关于要不要去。

normal.en: The th in the middle links it to other and either, its old partner.
normal.cn: 中间那个 th 把它与 other、either 这些老伙伴连在一起。

normal.en: If two branches end in the same place, the question becomes a concession.
normal.cn: 若两条岔路通向同一处，疑问就变成让步。

abstract.en: See a fork in a road with no map.
abstract.cn: 想一个没有地图的岔路口。

abstract.en: Hear two arrows pointing opposite ways.
abstract.cn: 听两支箭头指向相反方向。

abstract.en: Feel the doubt of a question that expects no answer.
abstract.cn: 感受一个并不期待回答的疑问。

examples.en: Please tell me whether the shop is still open.
examples.cn: 请告诉我那家店是否还开着。

examples.en: Whether she likes it or not, the rules must be followed.
examples.cn: 不管她喜不喜欢，规则都必须遵守。

examples.en: The only question is whether we have enough time.
examples.cn: 唯一的问题是时间够不够。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂泽」——站在岔路口朝两边各喂一声：去还是不去？

root: 古英语 hwæther / hwæder（两者中的哪一个）→ 中古英语 whether；同族有 either、other、whither。

sensesIntro.en: The word is born as a question about two things, turns into a neither-one-matters concession, and finally becomes the standard carrier of doubt.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词生来就是对两个事物的疑问，转成「哪个都无所谓」的让步，最后成为承载疑问的标准说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signpost with a yes arrow and a no arrow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块写着「是」与「否」两支箭头的路牌。

branches.en: The fork branch: he will come or he will not.
branches.cn: 岔路分支：他会来，或者不会来。

branches.en: The concession branch: whether by accident or design.
branches.cn: 让步分支：不管是偶然还是有意。

branches.en: The doubt branch: arguing about whether the plan is legal.
branches.cn: 存疑分支：争论计划是否合法。

branches.en: The grammar branch: whether after a preposition, never if.
branches.cn: 语法分支：介词之后用 whether，不用 if。

branches.en: The writing branch: careful prose keeps the full word.
branches.cn: 书面分支：严谨文章保留完整的词形。

intro.en: Whether is an old whole word, but its endings and its partners are transparent enough to take apart.
intro.cn: whether 是一个古老的整体词，不过它的词尾与搭档足够透明，可以拆开来看。

latinIntro.en: Latin marked a fork with utrum for the question and sive for the alternatives; the entries below are the borrowed counterparts, not ancestors of whether.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 utrum 表示疑问的分岔，用 sive 表示并列的选项；下面的条目是借入的对应词，并非 whether 的祖先。

items.example: It carries a fork in one word.
items.exampleCN: 它把岔口装在一个词里。

items.example: The same ending shows in other and either.
items.exampleCN: 同样的词尾出现在 other 和 either 中。

items.example: It answers the fork of whether.
items.exampleCN: 它回答了 whether 那个岔口。

items.example: It shares the ancient th ending.
items.exampleCN: 它共用了古老的 th 词尾。

items.example: It keeps the old wh question.
items.exampleCN: 它保留了古老的 wh 疑问。

items.example: It spells out the second branch.
items.exampleCN: 它把第二条岔路说出来。

items.example: It is the older and shorter form.
items.exampleCN: 这是更早也更短的形式。

items.example: It follows verbs such as decide.
items.exampleCN: 它跟在 decide 这类动词之后。
